**PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION --- PREPARED AT THE DIRECTION OF COUNSEL**

**CLEARWATER ENERGY HOLDINGS LLC** **INTERNAL MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** Priya Venkataraman, General Counsel, Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC

**FROM:** Michael Tran, Vice President of Construction, Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC

**DATE:** November 12, 2024

**RE:** Ridgeline Solar & Storage Facility --- Proposed Construction Sequence and Key Milestones

**CC:** Marcus Reyes, CEO, Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC; Catherine Amherst, Bridgeway Firth LLP (outside counsel)

**[1. Introduction and Purpose]{.underline}**

The purpose of this memorandum is to outline the proposed construction sequence, phasing plan, and key milestones for the Ridgeline Solar & Storage Facility (the \"Project\") in advance of the targeted construction Notice to Proceed (\"NTP\") on **January 15, 2025**. I am providing this memo to the legal team so that you and outside counsel can review the proposed timeline against all applicable permit conditions and advise on any adjustments before we finalize the construction management plan.

The Project consists of a 250 MW (AC) solar photovoltaic generating facility paired with a 100 MW / 400 MWh battery energy storage system (\"BESS\"), to be constructed on approximately 1,850 acres in Sections 14, 15, 22, and 23, Township 3 North, Range 24 West, Harmon County, Talmadge. The solar arrays will occupy approximately 1,450 acres, the BESS will be sited on an approximately 12-acre pad adjacent to the project substation, and we have planned three temporary laydown yards totaling 45 acres. A 345 kV gen-tie line of approximately 4.7 miles will connect the project substation to the Harmon County Substation, which is operated by Midplains Transmission Co.

We have now received all major regulatory approvals necessary to proceed with construction:

> • **CPCN** --- Docket No. PUC-2024-0347, issued October 18, 2024 (Talmadge Public Utilities Commission);
>
> • **TDEQ Environmental Compliance Order** --- ECO No. ENV-2024-1192, issued November 5, 2024 (Talmadge Department of Environmental Quality);
>
> • **FAA Determination of No Hazard** --- Aeronautical Study No. 2024-ASW-8851-OE, issued September 27, 2024 (Federal Aviation Administration); and
>
> • **Harmon County Special Use Permit** --- SUP No. HC-2024-0038, issued June 12, 2024.

Our target Commercial Operation Date (\"COD\") is **December 1, 2026**, providing a 24-month construction window from NTP. This timeline is tight but achievable with proper sequencing and coordination. Estimated total construction cost is approximately **\$412 million**, broken down as follows: \$268 million for the solar facility, \$102 million for the BESS, \$32 million for the gen-tie line and substation, and \$10 million in soft costs. We anticipate a peak construction workforce of approximately 400 workers, tapering down to 12 full-time employees during operations.

On the financing side, the capital stack is being finalized: a tax-equity commitment of \$235 million from Stonebridge Capital Markets LLC, a back-leverage term loan of \$130 million, and developer equity of \$47 million. NTP is contingent on financial close, which we are targeting for January 10, 2025. Jonathan Kressel at Stonebridge has indicated that his team will need the finalized construction schedule as part of their due diligence package, so I would like to get this nailed down promptly.

I respectfully request that you and Catherine Amherst at Bridgeway Firth review the proposed timeline set forth below against all permit conditions and advise on any areas where adjustments may be required.

**[2. Pre-Construction Activities (November 2024 -- January 2025)]{.underline}**

Several critical pre-construction activities are already underway or must be completed in the next two months to support the January 15, 2025 NTP:

**SWPPP Preparation and Filing.** The TDEQ ECO requires that our Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (\"SWPPP\") be submitted to the TDEQ at least 30 days before construction commencement. Our environmental team at Clearwater, working with our third-party consultant (Ridgecrest Environmental Services), is finalizing the SWPPP now. We are targeting submission to TDEQ by **December 15, 2024**, which should provide adequate lead time to support the January 15 NTP.

**TPUC 60-Day Prior Notice.** The CPCN requires that we provide 60 days\' advance written notice to the Talmadge Public Utilities Commission before the start of construction. Our team plans to file this notice on or about **November 15, 2024**. We are coordinating internally to ensure the notice includes all information required under the CPCN conditions.

**Pre-Construction Biological Surveys.** The TDEQ ECO requires biological surveys to be conducted within 60 days prior to ground disturbance for each construction phase. We are coordinating with Ridgecrest Environmental Services to complete the Phase 1 biological surveys across Sections 14, 15, 22, and 23. These surveys are expected to be completed by **late December 2024**, which will provide coverage for Phase 1 ground disturbance commencing in early February 2025.

**Glare Study.** We have retained SunPath Analytics to prepare the glare analysis required under the CPCN. The glare study is a technical analysis of potential glint and glare impacts on the Vance Municipal Airport (located approximately 6.2 miles southeast of the Project site) and surrounding roadways. SunPath has indicated that the report will be completed by **early February 2025**, and we will file it with the TPUC at that time.

**Interconnection Agreement with Midplains Transmission Co.** Negotiations with Midplains Transmission Co. regarding the terms of the Interconnection Agreement (\"IA\") for the 345 kV gen-tie interconnection at the Harmon County Substation are ongoing. Our interconnection team has been in discussions with Midplains since Q2 2024 on the commercial and technical terms. I am confident that the IA will be finalized in the coming weeks, though I should note that Midplains has been slow to respond on certain technical appendices related to system protection requirements and relay coordination studies. We continue to press for timely resolution and are escalating through Midplains\' management as needed.

**Site Access and Mobilization.** We plan to begin initial site access improvements, including grading of temporary access roads and establishment of the three laydown yards (totaling 45 acres across the northern, central, and southwestern portions of the site), in late January or early February 2025 following NTP. The access road improvements will utilize existing farm roads where possible and construct approximately 3.2 miles of new internal gravel roads.

**[3. Phase 1 --- Site Preparation and Solar Array Installation (February 2025 -- December 2025)]{.underline}**

**Scope.** Phase 1 encompasses all site preparation activities---clearing, grading, and internal road construction---as well as installation of the required vegetative screening buffer along the northern boundary of Sections 14 and 15. The TDEQ ECO requires a 50-foot vegetative screening buffer in this area, which is adjacent to the Pullman family homestead at 4200 County Road 118. Phase 1 also includes pile driving for single-axis tracker foundations, tracker assembly, and bifacial module installation across approximately 1,450 acres of the solar array footprint.

**Timeline Breakdown:**

> • **February -- March 2025:** Site clearing, rough grading, installation of erosion and sediment controls (silt fencing, sediment basins, stabilized construction entrances), access road construction, and laydown yard establishment. Vegetative screening buffer planting along the northern boundary will be initiated during this period, weather permitting, to give plantings the maximum time to establish before the next growing season.
>
> • **April -- May 2025:** Pile driving begins in Sections 22 and 23, the southern portions of the site. We are sequencing construction from south to north to keep initial heavy construction activities as far as possible from the Pullman homestead and other residences along County Road 118, minimizing early-stage construction impacts on adjacent landowners.
>
> • **June -- December 2025:** Tracker installation and module mounting will progress from south to north across the site. We anticipate the peak workforce of approximately **400 workers** during the August--October 2025 period, when multiple crews will be operating simultaneously across the array field.

**Dust Suppression.** The TDEQ ECO imposes a PM10 limit of 150 μg/m³ at the project boundary. We will deploy water trucks and, where necessary, chemical dust suppressants (magnesium chloride or equivalent) on active work areas and unpaved roads. Air quality monitoring stations will be installed along the northern and eastern site boundaries to provide continuous PM10 monitoring data.

**Quarterly Reports to TPUC.** The CPCN requires quarterly construction progress reports to the Talmadge Public Utilities Commission. Assuming construction begins in Q1 2025, the first quarterly report will be due **April 15, 2025**, with subsequent reports due on July 15, October 15, and so on throughout the construction period.

**BESS Foundation Work.** Foundation work for the 50 containerized BESS enclosures, located on the approximately 12-acre BESS pad adjacent to the project substation, will commence during Phase 1, approximately June--August 2025. This includes concrete pad construction, conduit installation, and grounding grid work to prepare the BESS pad for equipment installation beginning in Phase 3.

**[4. Phase 2 --- Gen-Tie Line and Substation Construction (Q2 2025 -- Q3 2025)]{.underline}**

**Scope.** Phase 2 covers the construction of the 345 kV gen-tie line (approximately 4.7 miles from the project substation to the Harmon County Substation operated by Midplains Transmission Co.) and the project substation itself.

**Gen-Tie Structure Details.** The gen-tie line will be supported by lattice steel towers and monopole structures reaching up to **180 feet above ground level (AGL)**, making these the tallest structures associated with the Project. Structures exceeding 150 feet AGL will require FAA obstruction lighting in accordance with AC 70/7460-1M. We will submit FAA Form 7460-2 (Notice of Actual Construction or Alteration) within 5 days of each such structure reaching its greatest height as required by the FAA Determination.

**Construction Cranes.** Erection of the tallest gen-tie structures will require cranes that may extend to heights exceeding 200 feet AGL during lifts. These cranes will require separate FAA aeronautical study filings, which must be submitted at least 45 days in advance of crane deployment. We will coordinate crane scheduling closely with the gen-tie erection sequence to ensure timely filings.

**Timeline.** Gen-tie construction is scheduled to begin in **April 2025** and be substantially complete by **September 2025**, providing a straightforward approximately six-month construction window for the 4.7-mile line and associated structures.

**Willow Creek Crossing.** The gen-tie route crosses Willow Creek, a perennial stream and tributary of the Red Fork River, as well as two county roads (CR-118 and CR-204). As required by the TDEQ ECO, the Willow Creek crossing will be constructed using a clear-span bridge design with no in-stream piers. We have scheduled the Willow Creek crossing work for **June -- August 2025**, as in-stream work must be performed during the June 1 -- September 30 window per TDEQ requirements to protect the Harmon Darter (*Etheostoma harmonensis*). This is a manageable window within the overall Phase 2 schedule, and the clear-span design should minimize the duration of work in the immediate creek vicinity.

**Substation Construction.** Concurrent with gen-tie construction, the project substation will be constructed on the approximately 12-acre BESS/substation pad from approximately April through August 2025. Major substation equipment---including the main power transformers, breakers, switchgear, and SCADA/communications systems---has been identified and procurement is underway as long-lead items.

**[5. Phase 3 --- BESS Installation and Commissioning (Q3 2025 -- Q3 2026)]{.underline}**

**Scope.** Phase 3 covers the installation of lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) battery modules in 50 containerized enclosures, along with power conversion systems (PCS), thermal management (HVAC), and fire suppression systems on the approximately 12-acre BESS pad. Foundation work completed during Phase 1 will allow BESS equipment installation to proceed immediately.

**Timeline:**

> • **September -- December 2025:** Battery module delivery and installation into containerized enclosures. PCS skid installation.
>
> • **January -- March 2026:** Electrical integration of BESS with the project substation, PCS testing, and HVAC commissioning.
>
> • **April -- June 2026:** Full BESS commissioning, including charge/discharge cycling, round-trip efficiency testing, and performance verification.

**Fire Suppression.** The BESS fire suppression system must comply with NFPA 855 and be certified by an independent third-party engineer prior to energization, as required by the TDEQ ECO. We are working with our fire suppression vendor (CleanAgent Fire Systems, Inc.) and plan to schedule the third-party certification inspection for **May 2026**, which will allow us to address any punch-list items before the BESS energization target.

**BESS Energization Target:** **July 2026.**

**[6. Phase 4 --- System Integration, Testing, and COD (Q3 2026 -- Q4 2026)]{.underline}**

**Scope.** Phase 4 is the final construction and commissioning phase, encompassing full system integration of the solar arrays, BESS, gen-tie line, and project substation, as well as interconnection testing with Midplains Transmission Co. at the Harmon County Substation.

**Timeline:**

> • **July -- September 2026:** Solar array energization, phased by section, beginning with Sections 22 and 23 (the first sections completed during Phase 1) and progressing northward.
>
> • **October -- November 2026:** Integrated system testing, grid synchronization with the Midplains system, and capacity testing. We will coordinate closely with Midplains on the interconnection testing schedule and protocols.
>
> • **Target COD: December 1, 2026.**

**Laydown Yard Restoration.** All three temporary laydown yards (45 acres total) must be restored to pre-construction condition within 180 days of COD per the TDEQ ECO. We plan to begin restoration work during Phase 4, starting approximately October 2026, so that the 180-day clock (running to approximately May 30, 2027) is comfortably met. Restoration will include re-grading, topsoil replacement, and reseeding with native grass species.

**Noise Compliance.** The CPCN imposes a 45 dBA noise limit at the nearest non-participating residence. We will coordinate with the equipment vendor during the inverter and BESS HVAC equipment selection process to ensure that equipment specifications comply with this limit at the relevant property-line measurement points. Post-energization noise testing will be performed by an independent acoustical consultant to confirm compliance.

**Post-COD Items.** Several obligations extend beyond COD: the decommissioning bond must be posted within 12 months of COD (by December 1, 2027); the first annual community benefit fund payment of \$150,000 is due on the first anniversary of COD (December 1, 2027), with payments continuing for 30 years; and the avian mortality monitoring program will run for 3 years post-COD, with annual reports due to TDEQ by March 1 of each year (first report due March 1, 2028).

**[7. Key Risks and Open Items]{.underline}**

Based on the construction team\'s assessment, the following key risks and open items should be monitored as we finalize the construction management plan:

**Weather and Seasonal Constraints.** The Willow Creek gen-tie crossing must be completed within the June 1 -- September 30 in-stream work window. We view this as manageable given the Phase 2 schedule, but it is weather-dependent and will require prioritization during the summer 2025 construction season.

**Supply Chain.** Battery modules (LFP cells sourced through our supply agreement with Jiangsu Greenpower Technology) and the main power transformers are long-lead items with current lead times of 12--16 months. We have placed preliminary orders but will need to finalize purchase orders promptly after financial close to protect delivery schedules.

**Midplains Transmission Co. Coordination.** As noted above, IA negotiations with Midplains are ongoing. Midplains\' responsiveness on the technical appendices---particularly the system protection requirements and relay coordination studies---has been a concern. We are hopeful the Interconnection Agreement will be finalized by early Q1 2025, but we are monitoring this closely and will escalate further if needed. The IA is a prerequisite to beginning gen-tie construction and interconnection testing, so further delays by Midplains could have downstream schedule impacts.

**Workforce Availability.** There is significant competition for skilled electrical and construction labor in the region, with at least two other utility-scale projects under construction in neighboring counties. We plan to begin recruitment efforts in December 2024 and are working with two regional labor contractors to secure commitments for the peak-workforce period.

**FAA Crane Filings.** Separate aeronautical study applications must be filed with the FAA at least 45 days in advance for any crane deployment exceeding 200 feet AGL. This requires careful coordination with the gen-tie erection schedule, and we will build these filing deadlines into the Phase 2 detailed schedule.

**Permitting Compliance.** The construction team will coordinate with legal and environmental consultants throughout the construction period to ensure all permit conditions are met. I would request that Priya and outside counsel at Bridgeway Firth LLP provide a comprehensive summary of all permit conditions and associated deadlines so that we can incorporate them into the construction management plan and assign responsibility for each compliance item.

**[8. Proposed Milestone Schedule]{.underline}**

The following table summarizes the key milestones for the Project:

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Milestone**                            **Target Date**
  ---------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  Financial Close                          January 10, 2025

  Construction NTP                         January 15, 2025

  TPUC 60-Day Construction Notice          November 15, 2024

  SWPPP Submission to TDEQ                 December 15, 2024

  Phase 1 Biological Survey Complete       Late December 2024

  Phase 1 Site Preparation Begins          February 1, 2025

  Glare Study Filed with TPUC              Early February 2025

  Interconnection Agreement Execution      Early Q1 2025 (negotiations ongoing)

  Phase 2 Gen-Tie Construction Begins      April 2025

  Willow Creek Crossing Construction       June -- August 2025

  Phase 2 Gen-Tie Substantially Complete   September 2025

  Phase 3 BESS Installation Begins         September 2025

  BESS Fire Suppression Certification      May 2026

  Phase 3 BESS Energization                July 2026

  Phase 4 Solar Energization (phased)      July -- September 2026

  Integrated System Testing                October -- November 2026

  **Target COD**                           **December 1, 2026**

  Laydown Yard Restoration Deadline        May 30, 2027 (180 days post-COD)

  Decommissioning Bond Posting             December 1, 2027 (12 months post-COD)

  First Community Benefit Fund Payment     December 1, 2027

  First Avian Monitoring Report to TDEQ    March 1, 2028
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This schedule assumes financial close on January 10, 2025, and NTP on January 15, 2025. Any delay to financial close or NTP would shift the downstream milestones accordingly and compress an already tight 24-month construction window.

**[9. Request for Legal Input]{.underline}**

I respectfully request that Priya and the Bridgeway Firth team review the proposed construction sequence and milestone schedule set forth in this memorandum against all conditions contained in the CPCN (Docket No. PUC-2024-0347), the TDEQ ECO (ECO No. ENV-2024-1192), the FAA Determination of No Hazard (Aeronautical Study No. 2024-ASW-8851-OE), and the Harmon County SUP (SUP No. HC-2024-0038). We need confirmation that the proposed timeline is compliant with all regulatory deadlines before we finalize the construction management plan and issue NTP.

I would like to schedule a meeting during the week of **November 18, 2024** to discuss any adjustments the legal team believes are necessary. Please let me know your availability. Note that we will be providing this memorandum and the proposed milestone schedule to Stonebridge Capital Markets LLC (Jonathan Kressel) as part of the financing due diligence package, so we should aim to resolve any open issues before that submission.

Please let me know if you need any additional information or if outside counsel has identified any permit conditions that require adjustments to our proposed schedule.

Michael Tran Vice President of Construction Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC michael.tran@clearwaterenergy.com (918) 555-0142

17	This matter comes before the Talmadge Public Utilities Commission (the \"Commission\" or \"TPUC\") upon the Application of Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC (\"Clearwater\" or \"Applicant\") for a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (\"CPCN\") to construct and operate the Ridgeline Solar & Storage Facility in Harmon County, Talmadge. Having reviewed the Application, the evidentiary record, the testimony and exhibits of the parties, the post-hearing briefs, and the applicable law, the Commission issues this Order granting a Conditional Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity, subject to the Conditions of Approval set forth herein.
18	
19	**[I. APPEARANCES]{.underline}**
20	
21	**For Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC (Applicant):**
22	
23	> Catherine Amherst, Lead Partner, and David Chu, Senior Associate, Bridgeway Firth LLP, One Riverwalk Center, Suite 3400, Ashford, Talmadge 73401.
24	
25	**For the Talmadge Public Utilities Commission Staff:**
26	
27	> James Orland, Senior Staff Analyst, Talmadge Public Utilities Commission, 1400 Capitol Plaza, Suite 600, Ashford, Talmadge 73402.
28	
29	**For Frank and Dorothy Pullman (Intervenors):**
30	
31	> Thomas Wakefield, Wakefield & Greer LLP, 210 Main Street, Suite 12, Hollis, Talmadge 73550, representing Frank and Dorothy Pullman, 4200 County Road 118, Hollis, Talmadge 73550.
32	
33	**For the Harmon County Board of Commissioners (Intervenor):**
34	
35	> Susan Milner, Harmon County Attorney\'s Office, 300 Courthouse Square, Hollis, Talmadge 73550.
36	
37	**[II. PROCEDURAL HISTORY]{.underline}**
38	
39	On March 15, 2024, Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC, a Delaware limited liability company registered to do business in the State of Talmadge, with its principal office at 900 Commerce Tower, Suite 2200, Ashford, Talmadge 73401, filed its Application for a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity to construct and operate the Ridgeline Solar & Storage Facility (the \"Project\" or the \"Facility\") in Harmon County, Talmadge. The Application was submitted pursuant to Talmadge Utility Code § 17-301 et seq. and TPUC Rule 165:35-31-1, and was accompanied by supporting documentation including engineering design plans, environmental assessments, financial pro formas, a decommissioning plan, and testimony from the Applicant\'s witnesses.
40	
41	On April 10, 2024, Clearwater initiated an Aeronautical Study with the Federal Aviation Administration (\"FAA\") under 14 C.F.R. Part 77 to evaluate the potential impact of the proposed Facility\'s structures on air navigation. The FAA assigned Aeronautical Study No. 2024-ASW-8851-OE to the review.
42	
43	On May 1, 2024, the Commission published notice of the Application in the Talmadge Register, Vol. 41, No. 17, in accordance with TPUC Rule 165:35-31-3. The notice described the nature and scope of the proposed Project, identified the location in Harmon County, and established a forty-five (45) day public comment period expiring on June 15, 2024. The Commission also directed the Applicant to publish notice in the Harmon County Herald, a newspaper of general circulation in Harmon County, for two consecutive weeks beginning May 3, 2024, and to post notice at the Harmon County Courthouse and at the Hollis Public Library. The Applicant confirmed compliance with all publication and posting requirements by affidavit filed May 22, 2024.
44	
45	During the public comment period, the Commission received twenty-three (23) written public comments. Fourteen (14) comments expressed support for the Project, citing economic benefits, clean energy production, and local tax revenue. Nine (9) comments expressed opposition or concern, raising issues related to noise, visual impacts, property values, impacts to agricultural land use, and potential effects on the Harmon Darter, a state-listed threatened fish species inhabiting Willow Creek. The Commission has reviewed and considered all public comments received.
46	
47	On May 20, 2024, Frank and Dorothy Pullman, owners of the residence and agricultural property at 4200 County Road 118, Hollis, Talmadge 73550, filed a Motion to Intervene through their counsel, Thomas Wakefield of Wakefield & Greer LLP. The Pullman family alleged that the Project would cause adverse noise, glare, and visual impacts to their homestead, which adjoins the northern boundary of the Project site, and that the proposed setbacks were insufficient to protect their property interests. On May 28, 2024, Administrative Law Judge Patricia Donahue granted the Motion to Intervene, finding that the Pullman family had demonstrated a direct and substantial interest in the proceeding sufficient to warrant intervention under TPUC Rule 165:5-3-4.
48	
49	On June 5, 2024, the Harmon County Board of Commissioners filed a Notice of Intervention as a governmental entity with direct regulatory authority over land use in the Project area, pursuant to TPUC Rule 165:5-3-5. The Commission acknowledged the County\'s intervention.
50	
51	On June 12, 2024, the Harmon County Board of Commissioners issued Special Use Permit No. HC-2024-0038 for the Project, authorizing the proposed solar energy use on the site subject to conditions specified therein, including setback, screening, and road improvement requirements.
52	
53	On July 22, 2024, the Talmadge Department of Environmental Quality (\"TDEQ\") completed its Environmental Impact Statement (\"EIS\") for the Project. The EIS evaluated potential impacts to water resources, wildlife habitat, air quality, noise, and visual aesthetics, and recommended mitigation measures including seasonal construction restrictions at Willow Creek and a vegetative screening buffer along certain Project boundaries.
54	
55	The evidentiary hearing in this matter was conducted before the Commission sitting en banc over four days, from August 12 through August 15, 2024, at the Commission\'s hearing room at 1400 Capitol Plaza, Ashford, Talmadge. During the hearing, the Commission received testimony and exhibits from the following witnesses: Marcus Reyes, Chief Executive Officer of Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC, who testified regarding the Project\'s purpose, design, financing, and public benefits; Dr. Elena Vasquez, P.E., Senior Vice President of Engineering at Clearwater, who testified regarding the Facility\'s engineering design, solar array layout, BESS configuration, and gen-tie line routing; Richard Henley, an independent acoustical consultant retained by Clearwater, who presented the results of the Applicant\'s noise impact study; James Orland, TPUC Senior Staff Analyst, who testified regarding Staff\'s independent review of the Application, the decommissioning cost estimate, and the ISIS; Frank and Dorothy Pullman, who testified regarding their concerns about noise, glare, dust, and the adequacy of proposed setbacks from their homestead; and Susan Milner, Harmon County Attorney, who testified regarding the County\'s issuance of the Special Use Permit and the County\'s position on land use compatibility and community benefits.
56	
57	On August 30, 2024, the evidentiary hearing concluded. The Commission established a briefing schedule requiring simultaneous post-hearing briefs to be filed by September 20, 2024, with reply briefs due by September 30, 2024. All parties timely submitted their post-hearing briefs and replies.
58	
59	On September 27, 2024, the FAA issued its Determination of No Hazard to Air Navigation for the Project (Aeronautical Study No. 2024-ASW-8851-OE), subject to conditions including marking and lighting requirements and a requirement that construction of the tallest structures commence on or before March 27, 2026.
60	
61	On October 1, 2024, the record in this proceeding was closed and the matter was taken under advisement by the Commission.
62	
63	**[III. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED FACILITY]{.underline}**
64	
65	The Ridgeline Solar & Storage Facility is a proposed utility-scale renewable energy generation facility comprising a 250 megawatt alternating current (\"MW (AC)\") solar photovoltaic generation facility combined with a 100 MW / 400 megawatt-hour (\"MWh\") battery energy storage system (\"BESS\"), together with an associated 345 kilovolt (\"kV\") generation-interconnection transmission line (the \"gen-tie line\").
66	
67	**Location and Acreage.** The Project is to be located on approximately 1,850 acres of land in Sections 14, 15, 22, and 23, Township 3 North, Range 24 West, Harmon County, Talmadge. The site is situated approximately 6.5 miles northwest of the town of Hollis, the county seat of Harmon County, and approximately 3.2 miles south of the unincorporated community of Gould. Access to the site is provided by County Road 118 from the north and County Road 204 from the east. The land is generally flat to gently rolling terrain, with elevations ranging from approximately 1,540 to 1,620 feet above mean sea level.
68	
69	**Solar Arrays.** The solar generation component will consist of single-axis tracker systems equipped with bifacial photovoltaic modules. The solar arrays will be deployed across approximately 1,450 acres of the 1,850-acre site. The tracker systems will be mounted on driven-pile foundations, and the maximum height of the arrays at full tracker tilt will not exceed fifteen (15) feet above ground level. The Applicant estimates the solar arrays will produce approximately 580,000 MWh of electricity annually, representing a capacity factor of approximately 26.5 percent.
70	
71	**Battery Energy Storage System.** The BESS component will consist of lithium-iron-phosphate (\"LFP\") battery modules housed in fifty (50) containerized enclosures, located on approximately twelve (12) acres of the site adjacent to the project substation. The BESS will have a rated capacity of 100 MW / 400 MWh, providing approximately four (4) hours of energy storage at full discharge. The BESS will be equipped with integrated thermal management, fire detection and suppression systems, and will be designed and operated in compliance with NFPA 855 and applicable local fire codes.
72	
73	**Gen-Tie Line and Substation.** The Project includes a 345 kV generation-interconnection transmission line of approximately 4.7 miles connecting the project substation to the Harmon County Substation, which is owned and operated by Midplains Transmission Co. The gen-tie line will be constructed on steel monopole structures with a maximum height of one hundred eighty (180) feet above ground level. The gen-tie line route crosses two county roads, CR-118 and CR-204, and one perennial stream, Willow Creek, a tributary of the Red Fork River. The Willow Creek crossing will utilize a clear-span bridge design with no in-stream piers to minimize impacts to aquatic habitat.
74	
75	**Temporary Construction Infrastructure.** Three temporary laydown yards totaling approximately 45 acres will be used during the construction period for staging of equipment, materials storage, and construction worker parking. The laydown yards will be decommissioned and restored following the completion of construction.
76	
77	**Workforce.** The Applicant estimates a peak construction workforce of approximately 400 workers over a construction period of approximately 24 months. Upon reaching Commercial Operation Date, the Facility will employ approximately 12 full-time permanent employees for operations and maintenance activities.
78	
79	**Project Cost and Financing.** The estimated total construction cost of the Project is Four Hundred Twelve Million Dollars (\$412,000,000), comprising approximately \$268 million for the solar generation facility, \$102 million for the BESS, \$32 million for the gen-tie line and project substation, and \$10 million in soft costs including permitting, engineering, legal, and development expenses. The Project is to be financed through a tax-equity and back-leverage structure arranged by Stonebridge Capital Markets LLC. The financing comprises a tax-equity commitment of \$235 million, a back-leverage term loan of \$130 million at the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (\"SOFR\") plus 225 basis points, and developer equity of \$47 million contributed by Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC. The aggregate financing sources of \$412 million are fully committed and sufficient to fund the total estimated project cost.
80	
81	**Target Schedule.** The Applicant has established a target Commercial Operation Date of December 1, 2026, with construction anticipated to commence in early 2025 following receipt of all required permits and a notice to proceed from the project lenders.
82	
83	**Applicant Background.** Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC is a regional renewable energy developer with a portfolio of 1.8 gigawatts of operating wind and solar assets across four states. The Ridgeline Solar & Storage Facility will be the Applicant\'s largest single project to date and its first project in the State of Talmadge.
84	
85	**Adjacent Landowners.** The Project site is bordered to the north by the property of Frank and Dorothy Pullman, whose homestead is located at 4200 County Road 118, Hollis, Talmadge 73550. The Pullman property adjoins the northern boundary of Sections 14 and 15 of the Project site. The nearest proposed solar array is located approximately 900 feet from the Pullman family residence.
86	
87	**[IV. FINDINGS OF FACT]{.underline}**
88	
89	Based upon the evidence of record, the testimony presented at the evidentiary hearing, the exhibits admitted into evidence, the post-hearing briefs of the parties, and the applicable law and regulations, the Commission makes the following findings of fact:
90	
91	**A. Public Need and Convenience**
92	
93	1\. The State of Talmadge has enacted the Talmadge Clean Energy Standards Act, Talmadge Utility Code § 17-201 et seq., which establishes a clean energy portfolio standard requiring that a minimum of forty percent (40%) of the electricity sold to retail customers in the state be generated from qualified renewable energy sources by the year 2035. As of the date of this Order, the state\'s current renewable energy generation capacity is insufficient to meet the 2035 target without substantial additional investment in renewable generation facilities and energy storage infrastructure.
94	
95	2\. The Ridgeline Solar & Storage Facility, with its 250 MW (AC) solar photovoltaic generation capacity and 100 MW / 400 MWh battery energy storage system, will make a significant and meaningful contribution to the state\'s progress toward meeting its clean energy portfolio standard. The BESS component, in particular, provides dispatchable clean energy and grid-balancing capabilities that are increasingly necessary as the penetration of variable renewable energy resources on the Talmadge grid continues to grow.
96	
97	3\. The Applicant has demonstrated its financial capability to construct and operate the Project through committed financing of \$385 million in tax-equity and back-leverage debt, arranged by Stonebridge Capital Markets LLC, supplemented by \$47 million in developer equity from Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC, for total committed project financing of \$412 million, which is equal to the estimated total project cost.
98	
99	4\. The Project will generate substantial employment benefits, including approximately 400 construction jobs during the 24-month construction period and 12 permanent full-time positions for facility operations and maintenance. These employment benefits will accrue primarily to the residents of Harmon County and surrounding communities.
100	
101	5\. The Commission finds that the proposed Facility will serve the public convenience and necessity by providing clean, reliable, and dispatchable electricity generation and storage capacity that contributes to the state\'s energy policy objectives and enhances the reliability and resilience of the Talmadge electric grid.
102	
103	**B. Site Suitability and Land Use**
104	
105	6\. The Project site is located on approximately 1,850 acres of agricultural land in Sections 14, 15, 22, and 23, Township 3 North, Range 24 West, Harmon County, Talmadge. The land is currently in row-crop cultivation and pasture use. The site topography is generally flat to gently rolling, and the solar resource at the site is well-suited for utility-scale solar photovoltaic generation.
106	
107	7\. The Harmon County Board of Commissioners issued Special Use Permit No. HC-2024-0038 on June 12, 2024, authorizing the proposed solar energy use on the Project site, subject to conditions specified in the SUP. The SUP includes, among other conditions, a seventy-five (75) foot setback requirement from all property lines, as represented by the Applicant during the evidentiary hearing. The issuance of the SUP confirms that the local land use authority has determined the proposed use to be compatible with surrounding land uses, subject to compliance with the SUP conditions.
108	
109	8\. The Talmadge Department of Environmental Quality completed its Environmental Impact Statement for the Project on July 22, 2024. The EIS concluded that, with appropriate mitigation measures, the Project\'s environmental impacts can be reduced to acceptable levels. The TDEQ\'s recommended mitigation measures include seasonal construction restrictions at Willow Creek, a vegetative screening buffer along certain Project boundaries, stormwater management requirements, and dust suppression measures. The TDEQ will memorialize its mitigation requirements in a separate Environmental Compliance Order (ECO No. ENV-2024-1192).
110	
111	9\. On September 27, 2024, the Federal Aviation Administration issued its Determination of No Hazard to Air Navigation (Aeronautical Study No. 2024-ASW-8851-OE), concluding that the proposed structures associated with the Facility do not constitute a hazard to air navigation, subject to conditions including marking and lighting requirements and a construction commencement deadline.
112	
113	10\. The nearest non-participating residence is the Pullman family homestead, located at 4200 County Road 118, Hollis, Talmadge 73550. The Pullman homestead is situated approximately 900 feet from the nearest proposed solar array along the northern boundary of Sections 14 and 15. The Commission has considered the Pullman family\'s concerns regarding the proximity of the Project to their residence and the potential for adverse impacts, and addresses those concerns in the conditions imposed herein and in Section V of this Order.
114	
115	**C. Environmental Considerations**
116	
117	11\. The TDEQ Environmental Impact Statement identified potential impacts to Willow Creek, a perennial stream and tributary of the Red Fork River, which flows through the Project area along the gen-tie line route. Willow Creek is documented habitat for the Harmon Darter (*Etheostoma harmonensis*), a species listed as threatened under the Talmadge Endangered Species Conservation Act, Talmadge Environmental Code § 29-401 et seq. The potential impacts to Willow Creek and the Harmon Darter arise primarily from the construction of the gen-tie line crossing of the stream, including potential sedimentation, habitat disturbance, and disruption of spawning activity.
118	
119	12\. To mitigate impacts to the Harmon Darter and its habitat, the TDEQ has recommended that construction of the gen-tie line crossing at Willow Creek be limited to the period of June 1 through September 30 of any calendar year. This seasonal construction window avoids the Harmon Darter\'s primary spawning period, which extends from early October through late May. The gen-tie line crossing shall utilize a clear-span bridge design with no in-stream piers, to minimize permanent alteration of the stream channel. The TDEQ\'s recommended mitigation measures will be memorialized in a separate Environmental Compliance Order (ECO No. ENV-2024-1192).
120	
121	13\. The Applicant presented a noise impact study prepared by Richard Henley, an independent acoustical consultant, which evaluated the anticipated operational noise levels generated by the Facility at the nearest non-participating residence. The noise study concluded that operational noise levels at the Pullman family homestead will not exceed 42 dBA (A-weighted) under typical operating conditions and 44 dBA (A-weighted) under worst-case operating conditions, accounting for the combined contributions of solar tracker motor drives, inverters, and BESS cooling systems. 165	**[V. DISCUSSION]{.underline}**
166	
167	**A. Standard of Review**
168	
169	Under Talmadge Utility Code § 17-301, the Commission shall issue a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity for the construction and operation of an electric generation facility upon finding that: (1) the proposed facility will serve the public convenience and necessity; (2) the proposed facility is consistent with the state\'s energy policy, including the clean energy portfolio standard established under Talmadge Utility Code § 17-201 et seq.; (3) the proposed facility will not unduly impact the natural environment; and (4) the proposed facility will not unduly impact the rights and interests of affected landowners and communities. The Applicant bears the burden of proof by a preponderance of the evidence on each of these statutory criteria. TPUC Rule 165:35-31-5 further specifies the information that must accompany a CPCN application, including engineering design plans, environmental assessments, financial documentation, a decommissioning plan, and evidence of compliance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements.
170	
171	The Commission has reviewed the Application and the entire evidentiary record in this proceeding against each of these statutory criteria and sets forth its analysis below.
172	
173	**B. Analysis of Public Need**
174	
175	The evidence in this proceeding demonstrates that the State of Talmadge faces a significant gap between its current renewable energy generation capacity and the capacity required to meet the forty percent (40%) clean energy portfolio standard by 2035. The Talmadge Energy Office\'s most recent biennial report, published in January 2024, estimates that the state will need to add approximately 4,500 MW of new renewable generation capacity and 1,200 MW of energy storage capacity between 2024 and 2035 to achieve compliance with the clean energy portfolio standard. The Ridgeline Solar & Storage Facility\'s 250 MW of solar generation capacity and 100 MW / 400 MWh of battery energy storage would represent approximately 5.5 percent of the identified renewable generation need and approximately 8.3 percent of the identified storage need.
176	
177	The BESS component of the Project provides particular value to the Talmadge grid. As the penetration of variable renewable energy resources increases, the need for dispatchable, fast-responding energy storage resources becomes more acute. The 100 MW / 400 MWh BESS will be capable of providing peak-shaving, frequency regulation, and capacity firming services that enhance grid reliability and reduce the need for fossil-fuel-fired peaking generation. The Commission views the integrated solar-plus-storage design of the Project as a significant advantage that differentiates it from standalone solar generation facilities.
178	
179	The Commission concludes that the Applicant has demonstrated by a preponderance of the evidence that the proposed Facility serves a clear and compelling public need for clean, reliable, and dispatchable electricity generation and storage capacity. This criterion is satisfied.
180	
181	**C. Environmental and Land Use Analysis**
182	
183	The Commission has carefully reviewed the TDEQ Environmental Impact Statement dated July 22, 2024, and the testimony of the parties regarding environmental and land use impacts. The Commission finds that the environmental impacts identified in the EIS can be adequately mitigated through the conditions imposed in this Order and the forthcoming TDEQ Environmental Compliance Order (ECO No. ENV-2024-1192).
184	
185	With respect to land use, the Commission notes that the Harmon County Board of Commissioners, as the local governmental authority with jurisdiction over land use in the Project area, issued Special Use Permit No. HC-2024-0038 on June 12, 2024, authorizing the proposed solar energy use on the site. The SUP contains conditions addressing local land use compatibility, including a reported seventy-five (75) foot setback from all property lines and other requirements regarding access roads, dust control, and visual screening. The Commission incorporates the SUP conditions by reference as conditions of this CPCN. The Applicant represented during the evidentiary hearing that the 75-foot SUP setback would govern the minimum distance between Project infrastructure and adjacent property boundaries, and that the Applicant intended to design the Facility\'s layout in compliance with this setback requirement.
186	
187	The TDEQ Environmental Impact Statement also requires a vegetative screening buffer of minimum fifty (50) feet in width along the northern boundary of Sections 14 and 15, adjoining the Pullman family homestead. This buffer is intended to mitigate visual and dust impacts on the Pullman property and is to consist of native species appropriate for the region. The Commission does not opine on whether the TDEQ\'s fifty-foot vegetative buffer and the Harmon County SUP\'s seventy-five-foot setback are cumulative or overlapping requirements, as that determination lies with TDEQ and Harmon County in the first instance. However, the Applicant is expected to comply with both requirements independen

The Commission has given careful consideration to the concerns raised by the Pullman family regarding operational noise from the Facility. The Pullman family\'s testimony described their concerns about noise from solar tracker motors, inverter stations, and BESS cooling systems, all of which will operate in close proximity to their homestead. The Applicant\'s noise study, prepared by acoustical consultant Richard Henley, concluded that operational noise at the Pullman residence will not exceed 42 dBA under typical conditions and 44 dBA under worst-case conditions. TPUC Staff confirmed that these estimates are reasonable. The Commission establishes a noise standard of forty-five (45) dBA (A-weighted, one-hour equivalent continuous sound level, Leq) measured at the property line of the nearest non-participating residence as the operational noise limit for the Facility. The Commission adopts this standard as a not-to-exceed limit. The 45 dBA limit provides a modest margin above the Applicant\'s worst-case estimate of 44 dBA, while remaining protective of the residential environment.

Regarding glare, the Commission requires that Clearwater complete a comprehensive glare analysis and file the results with the Commission within one hundred and twenty (120) days of the date of this Order. The glare analysis shall utilize the Sandia National Laboratories Solar Glare Hazard Analysis Tool or an equivalent methodology and shall evaluate potential impacts on nearby residences, public roads, and aviation facilities. If the analysis identifies significant adverse impacts, the Applicant shall propose mitigation measures for Commission review and approval.

**D. Interconnection and Transmission Analysis**

The Commission has reviewed the Interconnection System Impact Study submitted by the Applicant and is satisfied that the Project can be reliably interconnected to the Midplains Transmission Co. system at the Harmon County Substation via the proposed 4.7-mile, 345 kV gen-tie line. The ISIS demonstrates that the required system upgrades are minimal, technically feasible, and can be completed within the Project\'s construction timeline. Midplains Transmission Co.\'s July 8, 2024 letter to the Commission confirming substation capacity and upgrade feasibility provides additional assurance of interconnection viability.

However, the Commission is aware that Clearwater has not yet executed a definitive Interconnection Agreement with Midplains Transmission Co. The execution of such an agreement is a prerequisite to the commencement of construction of the gen-tie line and to the financial close of the Project, as the tax-equity and debt commitments are conditioned upon the existence of a binding interconnection arrangement. The Commission therefore requires that the Interconnection Agreement be executed within ninety (90) days of the effective date of this Order. This timeline is consistent with the representations of both Clearwater and Midplains Transmission Co. that negotiations are substantially advanced, and it allows adequate time for the resolution of any remaining commercial terms while maintaining the Project\'s overall schedule.

The Commission further notes the importance of maintaining the reactive power characteristics evaluated in the ISIS throughout the detailed engineering and construction process. The ISIS evaluated the Project\'s reactive power output at the point of interconnection under various operating scenarios and determined that the Project would maintain acceptable voltage support characteristics across the range of expected operating conditions. If material design changes during construction alter the Project\'s reactive power output by more than five percent (5%), the Applicant must file a revised ISIS for Commission review and approval prior to implementing such design change. This requirement ensures that the Commission and Midplains Transmission Co. can evaluate any significant changes to the Project\'s electrical characteristics that may affect transmission system reliability or the terms of the interconnection.

**E. Decommissioning Analysis**

The Commission has carefully reviewed the Applicant\'s decommissioning cost estimate of **Nineteen Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$19,200,000)**, as prepared by Grayson Engineering Group LLC. The estimate encompasses all reasonably anticipated costs of decommissioning the Facility at the end of its useful life, including removal of solar arrays, tracker systems, inverters, the BESS and containerized enclosures, the gen-tie line and structures, the project substation, access roads, and fencing; remediation of disturbed lands to pre-construction agricultural conditions; and disposal of battery storage components in compliance with applicable hazardous materials regulations. The estimate includes a fifteen percent (15%) contingency allowance.

TPUC Staff\'s independent review, as presented in the testimony of James Orland, confirmed that the decommissioning cost estimate is reasonable and consistent with industry standards for a solar photovoltaic and battery energy storage facility of this size, type, and location. Staff found no material deficiencies in the assumptions or methodology employed by Grayson Engineering Group LLC.

The Commission finds that a decommissioning bond in the form of an irrevocable standby letter of credit is the most appropriate form of financial assurance for the Facility. An irrevocable standby letter of credit provides immediate liquidity in the event of Applicant default, avoiding the delays and uncertainties associated with surety bond claims or reliance on the Applicant\'s general creditworthiness. The rating requirement of A- or higher from a nationally recognized statistical rating organization ensures that the issuing financial institution possesses adequate credit quality to honor the letter of credit when called. The Commission determines that the bond amount should be not less than the estimated decommissioning cost, and that the bond should be posted within twelve (12) months of the Commercial Operation Date and adjusted every five (5) years to reflect updated decommissioning cost estimates, subject to Commission review and approval.

**F. Construction Commencement and Timeline**

The Commission recognizes the Applicant\'s target Commercial Operation Date of December 1, 2026, and the associated construction timeline of approximately 24 months. The construction schedule is ambitious but achievable given the scale of the Project, the Applicant\'s experience with utility-scale renewable energy development, and the committed financing structure.

To ensure that the CPCN is exercised in a timely manner and that the authorized Facility is not indefinitely delayed, the Commission requires that construction commence within eighteen (18) months of the effective date of this Order. The effective date of this Order is October 18, 2024; accordingly, construction must commence no later than April 18, 2026. If construction has not commenced by that date, this CPCN shall automatically expire without further action by the Commission. The Applicant may seek an extension of the construction commencement deadline by filing a motion with the Commission demonstrating good cause for the delay, provided such motion is filed no later than sixty (60) days prior to the expiration of the deadline.

The Applicant shall provide written notice to the Commission at least sixty (60) days prior to the start of construction. The pre-construction notice shall include the anticipated date of the start of construction, a summary of all pre-construction conditions that have been satisfied, the name and contact information for the Applicant\'s on-site construction manager, and a copy of the fully executed Interconnection Agreement with Midplains Transmission Co.

For purposes of this Order, \"Commercial Operation Date\" or \"COD\" means the date on which the Facility first generates electricity for delivery to the grid. The Applicant shall provide written notice to the Commission within ten (10) business days of achieving the Commercial Operation Date. Numerous conditions of this Order are triggered by or measured from the Commercial Operation Date, including the decommissioning bond posting requirement and the commencement of community benefit fund payments. The Commission notes that its definition of COD for regulatory purposes may differ from the definition of commercial operation used in the Applicant\'s power purchase agreements, financing agreements, or other commercial contracts, and the Applicant should plan accordingly to ensure timely compliance with all conditions of this CPCN.

**[VI. CONCLUSIONS OF LAW]{.underline}**

Based on the foregoing Findings of Fact and Discussion, the Commission reaches the following conclusions of law:

1\. The Commission has jurisdiction over this matter and over the Applicant pursuant to Talmadge Utility Code § 17-101 et seq. and § 17-301 et seq., and TPUC Rule 165:35-31-1 et seq.

2\. The Applicant has met its burden of demonstrating, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the proposed Ridgeline Solar & Storage Facility will serve the public convenience and necessity, as required by Talmadge Utility Code § 17-301(A)(1).

3\. The Applicant has demonstrated that the proposed Facility is consistent with the state\'s energy policy, including the clean energy portfolio standard established under Talmadge Utility Code § 17-201 et seq., as required by Talmadge Utility Code § 17-301(A)(2).

4\. The Applicant has demonstrated compliance with applicable siting criteria under TPUC Rule 165:35-31-5, including the submission of adequate engineering design plans, environmental assessments, financial documentation, a decommissioning plan, and evidence of compliance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements.

5\. The issuance of a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity, subject to the Conditions of Approval set forth in Section VIII of this Order, is in the public interest.

6\. The CPCN shall be effective immediately upon issuance and shall remain in effect unless revoked, modified, or expired pursuant to its terms and the applicable provisions of the Talmadge Utility Code and TPUC Rules.

**[VII. ORDERING PARAGRAPHS]{.underline}**

**IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED** that a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity is hereby **GRANTED** to Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC to construct and operate the Ridgeline Solar & Storage Facility, a 250 MW (AC) solar photovoltaic generation facility with a 100 MW / 400 MWh battery energy storage system, and an associated 345 kV generation-interconnection transmission line of approximately 4.7 miles, located in Sections 14, 15, 22, and 23, Township 3 North, Range 24 West, Harmon County, Talmadge, subject to the Conditions of Approval set forth in Section VIII of this Order.

**IT IS FURTHER ORDERED** that this Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity is effective immediately as of October 18, 2024.

**IT IS FURTHER ORDERED** that Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC shall comply with each and every Condition of Approval set forth in Section VIII of this Order. **IT IS FURTHER ORDERED** that any party to this proceeding may seek rehearing or reconsideration of this Order by filing a motion with the Commission within thirty (30) days of the date of issuance of this Order, in accordance with TPUC Rule 165:5-9-1. The filing of a motion for rehearing or reconsideration shall not stay the effectiveness of this Order unless the Commission expressly orders otherwise.

**IT IS FURTHER ORDERED** that this Order shall be entered in the permanent records of the Commission and that copies shall be served upon all parties of record in this proceeding.

**Condition 18 --- Stormwater and Dust Control.** Clearwater shall implement a Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan and dust suppression plan in compliance with TDEQ requirements throughout the construction and operational life of the Facility. PM10 emissions shall not exceed 150 micrograms per cubic meter (μg/m³) at the Project boundary during construction. Clearwater shall maintain records of all dust suppression activities and stormwater management measures and make such records available to the Commission and TDEQ upon request.

**Condition 19 --- Pre-Construction Biological Surveys.** Clearwater shall conduct pre-construction biological surveys within sixty (60) days prior to ground disturbance for each phase of construction, in accordance with TDEQ requirements, to identify the presence of any state-listed threatened or endangered species, including the Harmon Darter (*Etheostoma harmonensis*). Survey results shall be filed with both TDEQ and the Commission within ten (10) business days of completion. If the surveys identify the presence of listed species in areas subject to ground disturbance, Clearwater shall coordinate with TDEQ to develop and implement appropriate avoidance or mitigation measures prior to commencing ground disturbance in the affected area.

**Condition 20 --- Willow Creek Crossing.** Construction of the gen-tie line crossing of Willow Creek shall be limited to the period of June 1 through September 30 of any calendar year, consistent with TDEQ requirements for the protection of the Harmon Darter (*Etheostoma harmonensis*). The crossing shall utilize a clear-span bridge design with no in-stream piers. Clearwater shall implement erosion and sedimentation controls during construction of the crossing in accordance with the TDEQ Environmental Compliance Order and shall restore any temporarily disturbed streambank areas within thirty (30) days of completing the crossing construction.

**Condition 21 --- Avian Mortality Monitoring.** Clearwater shall conduct annual avian mortality monitoring for a period of three (3) years following the Commercial Operation Date, using protocols and methodologies approved by TDEQ. Annual monitoring reports shall be submitted to TDEQ and the Commission by March 1 of each year following the monitoring period. If monitoring results indicate avian mortality rates significantly exceeding baseline levels, Clearwater shall consult with TDEQ to develop and implement additional mitigation measures.

**Condition 22 --- Compliance with Harmon County Special Use Permit.** This CPCN is expressly conditioned upon Clearwater\'s compliance with all conditions, restrictions, and requirements of Harmon County Special Use Permit No. HC-2024-0038, issued June 12, 2024, by the Harmon County Board of Commissioners. The conditions of SUP No. HC-2024-0038 are hereby incorporated by reference as if fully set forth herein. Any violation of the SUP shall constitute a violation of this CPCN and may be grounds for enforcement action under Section VII of this Order. In the event of any conflict between the conditions of this CPCN and the conditions of the SUP, the more restrictive requirement shall apply.

**Condition 23 --- Insurance and Indemnification.** Clearwater shall maintain comprehensive general liability insurance with minimum coverage of Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000) per occurrence and Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000) in the aggregate during both the construction and operational periods of the Facility. The Talmadge Public Utilities Commission, the State of Talmadge, and Harmon County shall be named as additional insureds on all such policies. Clearwater shall indemnify and hold harmless Harmon County, the State of Talmadge, and the TPUC from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, costs, and expenses, including reasonable attorney\'s fees, arising from the construction or operation of the Facility.

**Condition 24 --- Reporting of Material Changes.** Clearwater shall promptly notify the Commission of any material change in: (a) the design, capacity, or configuration of the Facility; (b) the financing structure, including any change in tax-equity investor, lender, or material financing terms; (c) the ownership or control of the Applicant; or (d) the Project timeline, including any delay in the anticipated Commercial Operation Date exceeding sixty (60) days. Material changes may require Commission review and approval prior to implementation, as determined by the Commission at its discretion.

**Condition 25 --- Transfer of CPCN.** This CPCN may not be transferred or assigned to any person or entity without the prior written approval of the Commission. Any change in the ownership or control of Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC that results in a new controlling entity, whether through merger, acquisition, reorganization, or otherwise, shall be deemed a transfer of this CPCN requiring Commission approval. An application for approval of a transfer shall be filed with the Commission at least ninety (90) days prior to the anticipated closing of any such transaction and shall include such information as the Commission may require to evaluate the proposed transferee\'s financial capability, managerial qualifications, and commitment to comply with the conditions of this CPCN.

**[IX. DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

For purposes of this Order, the following definitions shall apply:

**\"Applicant\"** or **\"Clearwater\"** means Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC, a Delaware limited liability company registered to do business in the State of Talmadge, with its principal office at 900 Commerce Tower, Suite 2200, Ashford, Talmadge 73401.

**\"BESS\"** means the battery energy storage system, consisting of lithium-iron-phosphate battery modules housed in fifty (50) containerized enclosures with a rated capacity of 100 MW / 400 MWh.

**\"Commission\"** or **\"TPUC\"** means the Talmadge Public Utilities Commission.

**\"Commercial Operation Date\"** or **\"COD\"** means the date on which the Facility first generates electricity for delivery to the grid.

**\"Facility\"** or **\"Project\"** means the Ridgeline Solar & Storage Facility, consisting of a 250 MW (AC) solar photovoltaic generation facility, a 100 MW / 400 MWh battery energy storage system, and an approximately 4.7-mile, 345 kV generation-interconnection transmission line, located in Sections 14, 15, 22, and 23, Township 3 North, Range 24 West, Harmon County, Talmadge.

**\"Gen-tie line\"** means the approximately 4.7-mile, 345 kV generation-interconnection transmission line connecting the project substation to the Harmon County Substation operated by Midplains Transmission Co.

**\"ISIS\"** means Interconnection System Impact Study.

**\"Order\"** means this Order Granting Conditional Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity, Docket No. PUC-2024-0347, dated October 18, 2024.

**\"TDEQ\"** means the Talmadge Department of Environmental Quality.

**\"FAA\"** means the Federal Aviation Administration.

**\"NRSRO\"** means a nationally recognized statistical rating organization, as defined in Section 3(a)(62) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.

**\"SUP\"** means Harmon County Special Use Permit No. HC-2024-0038, issued June 12, 2024.

**[X. SIGNATURE BLOCK]{.underline}**
