**[STATE OF TALMADGE]{.underline}**

**[TALMADGE DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY]{.underline}**

**[ENVIRONMENTAL COMPLIANCE ORDER]{.underline}**

**ECO No. ENV-2024-1192**

**In the Matter of:**

Application of Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC for Environmental Compliance Approval for the Ridgeline Solar & Storage Facility, Harmon County, Talmadge

**Date of Issuance:** November 5, 2024

**Issued by:** Dr. Nathan Suk, Director Talmadge Department of Environmental Quality 2100 Environmental Way Ashford, Talmadge 73403

**[I. RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS,** Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC (\"Clearwater\"), a Delaware limited liability company registered to do business in the State of Talmadge, with its principal office at 900 Commerce Tower, Suite 2200, Ashford, Talmadge 73401, submitted an application to the Talmadge Department of Environmental Quality (\"TDEQ\") for environmental review and compliance approval of the Ridgeline Solar & Storage Facility (the \"Project\" or \"Facility\"); and

**WHEREAS,** the Project consists of a 250 megawatt alternating current (250 MW AC) solar photovoltaic generation facility and a 100 megawatt / 400 megawatt-hour (100 MW / 400 MWh) battery energy storage system (\"BESS\") to be located on approximately 1,850 acres in Sections 14, 15, 22, and 23, Township 3 North, Range 24 West, Harmon County, Talmadge; and

**WHEREAS,** the Project includes a 345 kilovolt (345 kV) generation tie line (\"gen-tie line\") of approximately 4.7 miles connecting the Project to the Harmon County Substation, which is owned and operated by Midplains Transmission Co.; and

**WHEREAS,** the gen-tie line will cross two county roads, designated as County Road 118 (CR-118) and County Road 204 (CR-204), and one perennial stream, Willow Creek, a tributary of the Red Fork River; and

**WHEREAS,** the solar arrays consist of single-axis tracker systems with bifacial photovoltaic modules deployed across approximately 1,450 acres of the Project site, the BESS consists of lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) battery modules housed in 50 containerized enclosures on approximately 12 acres adjacent to the project substation, and three temporary laydown yards totaling approximately 45 acres will be utilized during the construction period for equipment staging, material storage, and workforce assembly; and

**WHEREAS,** the Project will employ approximately 400 workers during peak construction activities and approximately 12 full-time employees during ongoing commercial operations; and

**WHEREAS,** the TDEQ completed its Environmental Impact Statement (\"EIS\") for the Project on July 22, 2024, following a comprehensive review of the environmental, ecological, hydrological, and land-use impacts of the proposed Project; and

**WHEREAS,** the Talmadge Public Utilities Commission (\"TPUC\") issued a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity in Docket No. PUC-2024-0347 on October 18, 2024, authorizing the construction and operation of the Facility; and

**WHEREAS,** the Harmon County Board of Commissioners issued Special Use Permit No. HC-2024-0038 on June 12, 2024, granting conditional approval for the siting of the Facility within the unincorporated areas of Harmon County, Talmadge; and

**WHEREAS,** the Federal Aviation Administration issued a Determination of No Hazard to Air Navigation (Aeronautical Study No. 2024-ASW-8851-OE) on September 27, 2024, with respect to the structures and equipment associated with the Project; and

**WHEREAS,** the EIS identified potentially significant environmental impacts requiring mitigation, including impacts to aquatic habitat (specifically Willow Creek and the state-listed threatened Harmon Darter, *Etheostoma harmonensis*), terrestrial habitat, avian species, stormwater management, air quality, visual resources, cultural and archaeological resources, and fire safety associated with the BESS component; and

**WHEREAS,** the TDEQ has authority under the Talmadge Environmental Quality Act, T.S.A. §§ 27A-1-101 *et seq.*, and the regulations promulgated thereunder, to impose conditions on projects subject to environmental review in order to mitigate identified environmental impacts to acceptable levels; and

**WHEREAS,** Clearwater has reviewed the conditions set forth herein and has agreed to comply with such conditions as a condition of environmental compliance approval for the Project.

**[II. FINDINGS]{.underline}**

Based upon its review of the application, the Environmental Impact Statement, supplemental materials, public comments, and all other evidence and information in the administrative record, the Director of the Talmadge Department of Environmental Quality hereby makes the following Findings:

**Finding 1.** The TDEQ has reviewed the complete application, the Environmental Impact Statement dated July 22, 2024, all supplemental materials submitted by Clearwater, public comments received during the EIS public comment period, and all other relevant evidence and information in the administrative record for the Project. The TDEQ has determined that the record is sufficient to support the issuance of this Environmental Compliance Order.

**Finding 2.** The Project site contains and is adjacent to environmentally sensitive areas, including Willow Creek, a perennial stream and tributary of the Red Fork River, which provides documented habitat for the Harmon Darter (*Etheostoma harmonensis*), a species listed as threatened under the Talmadge Endangered and Threatened Species Act, T.S.A. § 29-2-101 *et seq.* The EIS confirmed the presence of a reproducing population of the Harmon Darter in the reach of Willow Creek within and immediately adjacent to the Project site.

**Finding 3.** The Project will result in land disturbance across a significant area of previously undeveloped agricultural and pasture land in Harmon County. The TDEQ has calculated the total disturbed acreage subject to mitigation as 1,495 acres, consisting of the following components:

> \(a\) Approximately 1,450 acres for the solar photovoltaic array installation, including single-axis tracker systems, associated grading, access roads internal to the solar array fields, and inverter pad areas; and
>
> \(b\) Approximately 45 acres for three (3) temporary laydown yards to be utilized during the construction period for equipment staging, material storage, and workforce mobilization.
>
> **Total Disturbed Acreage Subject to Mitigation: 1,495 acres.**

**Finding 4.** Construction activities near Willow Creek, particularly the installation of the gen-tie line crossing and associated grading and vegetation clearing within the riparian corridor, have the potential to adversely affect the Harmon Darter (*Etheostoma harmonensis*) and its habitat through increased sedimentation, turbidity, and direct disturbance of stream substrate if not restricted to appropriate seasonal windows and conducted in compliance with best management practices for aquatic resource protection.

**Finding 5.** The BESS component of the Project involves the storage of significant quantities of energy in lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) battery modules housed within 50 containerized enclosures on approximately 12 acres. The storage and operation of LFP battery systems present fire safety risks, including the potential for thermal runaway events, and environmental contamination risks associated with the release of battery electrolytes, off-gases, or firefighting agents. These risks require the installation of specialized fire detection, suppression, and containment systems, as well as independent third-party certification of such systems prior to energization.

**Finding 6.** The Project is located adjacent to the Pullman family homestead at 4200 County Road 118, Hollis, Talmadge 73550, along the northern boundary of Sections 14 and 15, Township 3 North, Range 24 West, Harmon County. The proximity of the solar array installation to this occupied residential property necessitates visual screening measures to mitigate aesthetic impacts, including the establishment of a vegetative buffer along the northern Project boundary.

**Finding 7.** The TDEQ finds that, subject to the conditions set forth in this Order, the environmental impacts of the Project can be mitigated to acceptable levels consistent with the standards and objectives of the Talmadge Environmental Quality Act, T.S.A. §§ 27A-1-101 *et seq.*, and the regulations promulgated thereunder.

**Finding 8.** The term \"construction commencement\" as used in this Order refers to the initiation of any physical ground-disturbing activity at the Project site, including but not limited to grading, excavation, trenching, vegetation clearing, topsoil stripping, road construction, foundation installation, and any other activity that results in the physical disturbance of the land surface.

**Finding 9.** For purposes of this Order, \"Commercial Operation Date\" or \"COD\" shall mean the date on which all components of the Facility --- including the solar photovoltaic array, the battery energy storage system, the project substation, and the gen-tie line --- have been fully installed, tested, and commissioned for commercial service in accordance with applicable industry standards and interconnection requirements.

**[III. ORDER]{.underline}**

**NOW, THEREFORE,** based on the foregoing Recitals and Findings, and pursuant to the authority vested in the Director of the Talmadge Department of Environmental Quality under the Talmadge Environmental Quality Act, T.S.A. §§ 27A-1-101 *et seq.*, and the regulations promulgated thereunder, it is hereby **ORDERED** as follows:

**[IV. CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL]{.underline}**

**Condition 1: General Compliance**

Clearwater shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, ordinances, and requirements relating to environmental protection in connection with the construction, operation, maintenance, and eventual decommissioning of the Project. Compliance with this Order does not relieve Clearwater of its independent obligation to obtain and comply with any other permits, approvals, licenses, or authorizations that may be required by any federal, state, or local governmental authority, including but not limited to the United States Army Corps of Engineers, the United States Fish and Wildlife Service, the Talmadge Corporation Commission, and the Harmon County Board of Commissioners.

**Condition 2: Pre-Construction Biological Survey**

Clearwater shall conduct a pre-construction biological survey of each area proposed for ground disturbance no earlier than sixty (60) days prior to the commencement of ground-disturbing activities in that area. The survey shall be conducted by a qualified biologist holding appropriate credentials and approved in advance by the TDEQ. The biological survey shall identify the presence or absence of any state-listed threatened or endangered species, including but not limited to the Harmon Darter (*Etheostoma harmonensis*), as well as any critical or sensitive habitat, nesting sites, or other ecological features of significance. Survey results, together with the biologist\'s written findings and recommendations, shall be submitted to the TDEQ at the attention of Rebecca Tannenbaum, Environmental Review Specialist, at 2100 Environmental Way, Ashford, Talmadge 73403, no later than thirty (30) days prior to ground disturbance in the surveyed area. If any state-listed threatened or endangered species or critical habitat is identified within or immediately adjacent to the proposed disturbance area, Clearwater shall not proceed with ground-disturbing activities in the affected area until a supplemental mitigation plan has been prepared by Clearwater and approved in writing by the TDEQ. Separate biological surveys shall be conducted for each construction phase and each discrete area of ground disturbance, and no single survey shall be relied upon to satisfy this Condition for areas not included within the geographic scope of that survey.

**Condition 3: Willow Creek Crossing Restrictions**

Due to the documented presence of the Harmon Darter (*Etheostoma harmonensis*), a species listed as threatened under the Talmadge Endangered and Threatened Species Act, T.S.A. § 29-2-101 *et seq.*, in Willow Creek (a perennial stream and tributary of the Red Fork River), all construction activities within the Willow Creek riparian corridor --- including but not limited to installation of the gen-tie line crossing structure, grading, vegetation clearing, equipment staging, and any other physical disturbance within 100 feet of the ordinary high water mark of Willow Creek --- shall be restricted to the period of June 1 through September 30 of any calendar year. No construction activity of any kind shall occur within the Willow Creek riparian corridor outside of this permitted seasonal window without prior written authorization from the TDEQ.

The gen-tie line crossing of Willow Creek shall be designed and constructed as a clear-span bridge or aerial crossing with no in-stream piers, pilings, footings, or other permanent structures placed within the stream channel or below the ordinary high water mark. All structural supports shall be located outside the stream channel and above the ordinary high water mark.

During the permitted construction window of June 1 through September 30, Clearwater shall implement continuous turbidity monitoring at stations located upstream and downstream of the Willow Creek crossing site, with monitoring results recorded and reported to the TDEQ on a weekly basis throughout the duration of construction activities within the riparian corridor. Any exceedance of a 50 Nephelometric Turbidity Units (NTU) increase above background turbidity levels, as measured at the downstream monitoring station relative to the upstream control station, shall require the immediate cessation of all in-stream and near-stream construction work and notification to the TDEQ within twenty-four (24) hours of the exceedance event. Work shall not resume until turbidity levels have returned to within 50 NTU of background levels and the TDEQ has been notified.

**Condition 4: Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP)**

Clearwater shall prepare and submit a comprehensive Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (\"SWPPP\") to the TDEQ no later than thirty (30) days before construction commencement. The SWPPP shall be prepared in accordance with TDEQ Stormwater Management Regulations, T.A.C. § 252:606, and shall address, at a minimum, the following elements: erosion and sediment control measures for all phases of construction; construction sequencing and phasing schedules; temporary and permanent stormwater management facilities, including detention basins and drainage conveyances; spill prevention and response procedures for fuels, lubricants, and other potentially hazardous materials; and comprehensive monitoring protocols for stormwater discharge quality and quantity. The SWPPP shall cover the entire 1,850-acre Project site, including all solar array areas, the BESS area, temporary laydown yards, the gen-tie line corridor, and all access roads, both temporary and permanent. The TDEQ shall review and either approve or request revisions to the SWPPP within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of the complete SWPPP submission. Construction commencement shall not occur until the SWPPP has been approved in writing by the TDEQ. Clearwater shall maintain the SWPPP on-site at all times during construction and shall update the SWPPP as necessary to reflect changes in construction activities, sequencing, or site conditions.

**Condition 5: Dust Suppression and Air Quality**

Clearwater shall implement a dust suppression plan throughout the construction period sufficient to ensure that particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter of 10 micrometers or less (PM10) does not exceed 150 micrograms per cubic meter (μg/m³) at any point along the Project boundary, as measured using TDEQ-approved monitoring equipment and methodology. Clearwater shall install no fewer than four (4) PM10 monitoring stations at the Project boundary, with one station positioned on each cardinal side of the Project site (north, south, east, and west), and shall maintain continuous monitoring data logs that are available for TDEQ inspection during all business hours and upon reasonable request. Dust suppression measures implemented by Clearwater may include, but are not limited to, the deployment of water trucks for application to active construction areas and unpaved roads, the use of chemical dust suppressants approved by the TDEQ, gravel surfacing of temporary and permanent access roads, the imposition of speed restrictions for all construction vehicles and equipment on unpaved surfaces, and the covering or stabilization of exposed soil stockpiles. If any PM10 monitoring station records a reading that exceeds the 150 μg/m³ threshold, Clearwater shall immediately cease all dust-generating construction activities within 500 feet of the location of the exceedance and shall notify the TDEQ within twenty-four (24) hours. Dust-generating activities in the affected area shall not resume until Clearwater has implemented additional suppression measures and confirmed that PM10 levels have returned to compliance.

**Condition 6: Vegetative Screening Buffer**

Clearwater shall establish and maintain a vegetative screening buffer of a minimum width of fifty (50) feet along the entire northern boundary of Sections 14 and 15, Township 3 North, Range 24 West, Harmon County, Talmadge, adjoining the Pullman family homestead at 4200 County Road 118, Hollis, Talmadge 73550. The vegetative screening buffer shall consist of native species plantings appropriate for the climate and soil conditions of Harmon County, including a mix of evergreen and deciduous trees and shrubs selected to provide year-round visual screening. Plantings shall be installed at a density and arrangement sufficient to achieve a minimum of eighty percent (80%) visual opacity within three (3) years of planting, as determined and certified by a licensed landscape architect retained by Clearwater.

Clearwater shall submit a detailed vegetative screening plan to the TDEQ for review and approval no later than sixty (60) days prior to the commencement of planting activities. The screening plan shall include plant species, sizes at time of planting, spacing, planting density, irrigation provisions for the establishment period, and a maintenance schedule. Planting of the vegetative screening buffer shall be completed prior to the commencement of solar array installation in Sections 14 and 15. Clearwater shall maintain the vegetative buffer in good condition for the entire operational life of the Project, including regular inspection, watering during drought conditions, and replacement of any dead, diseased, or significantly damaged plantings within one (1) growing season of identification.

**Condition 7: Erosion and Sediment Control**

Clearwater shall install and maintain erosion and sediment control measures in accordance with the TDEQ Best Management Practices Manual (Publication No. TDEQ-BMP-2022) throughout the construction period and continuing until all disturbed areas have been permanently stabilized through revegetation, paving, or other approved stabilization methods. Silt fences, sediment basins, check dams, temporary seeding, erosion control blankets, and other appropriate erosion control devices shall be installed and fully operational before any ground-disturbing activity begins in each construction phase or area. Clearwater shall inspect all erosion and sediment control measures at least weekly during the construction period and within twenty-four (24) hours following any precipitation event exceeding 0.5 inches of rainfall over a 24-hour period, as measured at the nearest on-site or TDEQ-approved rain gauge. All inspection findings, including the condition of each erosion control device, any deficiencies identified, and corrective actions taken, shall be documented in written inspection logs maintained on-site and available for TDEQ review upon request.

**Condition 8: Wetland and Waterway Protection**

Clearwater shall avoid all wetlands and waterways on the Project site except as specifically authorized under this Order --- namely, the Willow Creek crossing authorized under Condition 3 above. No fill material, construction debris, spoils, or heavy equipment shall be placed, stored, or operated in any wetland or waterway on or adjacent to the Project site. Any inadvertent discharge of sediment, construction materials, fuels, or other substances into a wetland or waterway shall be reported to the TDEQ within twenty-four (24) hours of discovery and shall be remediated promptly in accordance with a corrective action plan submitted to and approved by the TDEQ. The gen-tie line alignment shall maintain a minimum horizontal setback of fifty (50) feet from the delineated boundary of all wetlands on or adjacent to the Project site, except at the authorized Willow Creek crossing point specified in Condition 3. Wetland boundaries shall be delineated by a qualified wetland scientist in accordance with the methodology set forth in the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Wetlands Delineation Manual.

**Condition 9: Environmental Mitigation Fee**

Clearwater shall pay to the TDEQ an annual environmental mitigation fee calculated at the rate of Two Dollars and Seventy-Five Cents (\$2.75) per disturbed acre per year. For purposes of this Condition, the total disturbed acreage is calculated as follows:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Component**                       **Acreage**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Solar array installation area       1,450 acres

  Temporary laydown yards (3 yards)   45 acres

  **Total Disturbed Acreage**         **1,495 acres**
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

> **Annual Environmental Mitigation Fee:** 1,495 acres × \$2.75/acre = **\$4,111.25 per year.**

The mitigation fee shall be due and payable on or before January 31 of each calendar year, beginning with the first January 31 following construction commencement (as defined in Finding 8 of this Order), and shall continue annually for the duration of the construction period and the first five (5) years of Project operations following the Commercial Operation Date. Payments shall be made by check or wire transfer to the TDEQ Environmental Mitigation Fund, Account No. 7740-EMF-2024 (or such other account number as the TDEQ may designate in writing). Clearwater shall include with each payment a written statement identifying the ECO number, the payment period, and the acreage basis for the calculation. Failure to timely pay the annual environmental mitigation fee may result in the issuance of a stop-work order, assessment of late fees and interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, or other enforcement action as authorized under T.S.A. § 27A-1-401.

**Condition 10: Temporary Laydown Yard Restoration**

All three (3) temporary laydown yards, totaling approximately 45 acres, shall be restored to pre-construction condition within one hundred eighty (180) days of the Commercial Operation Date (\"COD\") as defined in Finding 9 of this Order. Restoration activities shall include, at a minimum, the removal of all temporary structures, gravel, construction debris, and hazardous materials from each laydown yard site; regrading of the land surface to match pre-construction contours as documented in the baseline topographic survey; replacement of topsoil to a minimum depth of six (6) inches using stockpiled or imported topsoil of comparable quality; and reseeding of the restored area with a TDEQ-approved native seed mix appropriate for the soil and climate conditions of Harmon County. Clearwater shall submit a Laydown Yard Restoration Plan to the TDEQ for review and approval no later than ninety (90) days prior to the anticipated COD. The Restoration Plan shall include a detailed schedule, grading plans, topsoil specifications, seed mix composition and application rates, and success criteria for revegetation. A final restoration inspection shall be conducted jointly by representatives of Clearwater and the TDEQ within thirty (30) days after the completion of all restoration activities at each laydown yard site. The TDEQ shall issue written confirmation of satisfactory restoration upon successful completion of the joint inspection.

**Condition 11: Hazardous Materials Management**

Clearwater shall prepare and maintain a Hazardous Materials Management Plan (\"HMMP\") throughout the construction and operation of the Project. The HMMP shall comprehensively address the storage, handling, transportation, use, and disposal of all hazardous materials used in connection with the Project, including but not limited to battery electrolytes and related chemical compounds, transformer oils and insulating fluids, hydraulic fluids, diesel and gasoline fuels, lubricants, cleaning solvents, and any other substances classified as hazardous under applicable federal or state law. The HMMP shall be submitted to the TDEQ for review and approval no later than thirty (30) days before construction commencement. All hazardous materials storage areas shall be equipped with secondary containment systems capable of holding a minimum of one hundred ten percent (110%) of the volume of the largest individual container stored within the containment area. Spill response kits, including absorbent materials, containment booms, and personal protective equipment, shall be maintained at each hazardous materials storage location and at the BESS enclosure area at all times during construction and operations.

**Condition 12: Avian Mortality Monitoring**

Clearwater shall implement a comprehensive avian mortality monitoring program for a period of three (3) years following the Commercial Operation Date. Monitoring shall be conducted by a qualified avian biologist holding appropriate credentials and approved in advance by the TDEQ, in accordance with the TDEQ Avian Monitoring Protocol (Publication No. TDEQ-AMP-2021). The monitoring area shall encompass the entire 1,850-acre Project site and a 500-foot buffer zone extending beyond the Project boundary in all directions. Monitoring activities shall include systematic carcass searches conducted at a minimum frequency of biweekly (every two weeks) during spring and fall migration periods, defined as March 1 through May 31 and August 15 through November 15, respectively, and monthly during all other periods of the year. Search plots shall be distributed across representative portions of the solar array, BESS area, gen-tie line corridor, and buffer zone in accordance with the sampling methodology specified in the TDEQ Avian Monitoring Protocol.

Annual monitoring reports shall be submitted to the TDEQ no later than March 1 of each year following the monitoring year. The first annual report shall be due on the first March 1 that falls at least six (6) months after the Commercial Operation Date. Each annual report shall include a summary of all carcasses and injured birds detected, species identification, estimated cause of mortality, searcher efficiency and carcass persistence trial results, and statistically adjusted mortality estimates.

If monitoring results indicate that avian mortality rates exceed the thresholds established in the TDEQ Avian Monitoring Protocol, the TDEQ may require Clearwater to implement additional mitigation measures at Clearwater\'s expense, which may include but are not limited to curtailment of facility operations during peak migration periods, installation of bird flight diverters on the gen-tie line, modification of lighting at the facility, or other adaptive management measures as determined by the TDEQ to be appropriate and effective.

**Condition 13: Noise and Vibration During Construction**

Construction activities producing noise levels in excess of 75 dBA, as measured at the nearest non-participating residence using a Type 1 or Type 2 sound level meter, shall be limited to the hours of 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., Monday through Saturday. No construction activity producing noise in excess of 75 dBA at the nearest non-participating residence shall occur on Sundays or state-recognized holidays. Clearwater shall provide advance written notice to all non-participating residences located within 1,000 feet of active construction areas at least seven (7) calendar days before the commencement of major construction phases, including but not limited to pile driving for solar array foundations, operation of heavy earthmoving equipment, and concrete pouring. The written notice shall identify the nature of the construction activity, the expected duration, and a contact person for noise complaints. Blasting, if required for any purpose in connection with the Project, shall require separate written approval from the TDEQ and shall be subject to additional conditions as the TDEQ may impose.

**Condition 14: Cultural and Archaeological Resources**

Clearwater shall implement an Unanticipated Discovery Plan (\"UDP\") for the protection of cultural and archaeological resources throughout the construction period. The UDP shall be prepared in consultation with the Talmadge State Historic Preservation Office (\"SHPO\") and shall be submitted to the TDEQ for approval prior to construction commencement. If any cultural artifacts, human remains, or archaeological features are encountered during construction activities at any location on the Project site, Clearwater shall immediately cease all work within 100 feet of the discovery location and shall notify the TDEQ and the Talmadge SHPO within twenty-four (24) hours of the discovery. The discovery site shall be secured and protected from further disturbance pending evaluation. Work in the discovery area shall not resume until Clearwater has received written authorization from the TDEQ, in consultation with the SHPO, to proceed.

**Condition 15: BESS Fire Suppression and Safety**

The Battery Energy Storage System fire suppression and safety system shall be designed, installed, and maintained in compliance with NFPA 855 and all applicable provisions of the Talmadge Fire Prevention Code. The fire suppression system for the BESS shall include, at a minimum, the following components:

> \(a\) Automatic fire detection systems installed in each of the fifty (50) containerized BESS enclosures, including thermal sensors capable of detecting abnormal temperature rise and smoke detection devices;
>
> \(b\) An automatic fire suppression system --- utilizing clean agent, water mist, or another suppression technology approved by the TDEQ --- installed in each containerized BESS enclosure and designed to activate automatically upon detection of a fire event;
>
> \(c\) Thermal runaway containment measures for each BESS enclosure, including adequate mechanical ventilation systems designed to manage and vent combustible gases, gas detection systems capable of detecting hydrogen, carbon monoxide, and other off-gases associated with LFP battery thermal events, and physical barriers between battery modules as specified in NFPA 855;
>
> \(d\) An on-site fire water supply with a minimum storage capacity of fifty thousand (50,000) gallons, connected to hydrants and hose connections accessible to the Harmon County Fire Department and any other responding fire suppression personnel; and
>
> \(e\) Thermal monitoring systems capable of continuously monitoring the temperature of individual battery modules or module strings and providing remote alarm notification to Clearwater\'s operations center and the local emergency dispatch.

The BESS fire suppression system shall be certified by an independent third-party fire protection engineer, licensed in the State of Talmadge, prior to the energization of any BESS component. The independent certification shall confirm that the BESS fire suppression system, as designed and installed, complies with NFPA 855 and the Talmadge Fire Prevention Code and is adequate to detect, suppress, and contain fire events, including thermal runaway propagation events, within the BESS enclosures. A copy of the independent third-party certification shall be filed with the TDEQ no later than fifteen (15) calendar days prior to BESS energization.

Clearwater shall coordinate with the Harmon County Fire Department to develop a comprehensive BESS Emergency Response Plan (\"ERP\"), which shall address emergency response procedures for thermal runaway events, battery fires, hazardous material releases, and other BESS-related emergencies. The ERP shall include site access maps, equipment locations, battery chemistry information, recommended suppression tactics, and personal protective equipment requirements for first responders. The ERP shall be submitted to the TDEQ and the Harmon County Fire Department for review and approval no later than sixty (60) days prior to BESS energization.

**Condition 16: Reporting and Record-Keeping**

Clearwater shall maintain all environmental monitoring records, inspection logs, biological survey results, laboratory reports, and compliance documentation on-site in a centralized location accessible to TDEQ inspectors, and shall make such records available for TDEQ inspection at all times during the construction period and for a period of five (5) years following the Commercial Operation Date. Clearwater shall provide the TDEQ with written notification of construction commencement within five (5) business days of the initiation of any ground-disturbing activity at the Project site. Such notification shall identify the date of construction commencement, the location and nature of the initial ground-disturbing activity, and the name and contact information for the on-site construction manager. Clearwater shall submit semi-annual environmental compliance reports to the TDEQ during the construction period, with reports due on January 31 and July 31 of each calendar year in which construction activities occur. Each semi-annual report shall summarize Clearwater\'s compliance status with respect to each condition of this Order, identify any deviations, incidents, or corrective actions, and include copies of all monitoring data collected during the reporting period.

**Condition 17: Third-Party Environmental Monitor**

Clearwater shall retain, at its own expense, an independent third-party environmental monitor (the \"Environmental Monitor\") approved by the TDEQ to oversee compliance with the conditions of this Order during the construction period. The Environmental Monitor shall be an individual or firm with demonstrated expertise in environmental compliance monitoring for large-scale energy infrastructure projects and shall be independent of Clearwater and its contractors. The Environmental Monitor shall have authority to temporarily halt construction activities if, in the Monitor\'s professional judgment, an imminent violation of any condition of this Order is occurring or is reasonably likely to occur. The Environmental Monitor shall submit monthly reports directly to the TDEQ, with copies provided to Clearwater, summarizing construction activities conducted during the reporting period, compliance status with respect to each applicable condition of this Order, and any incidents, deviations, or corrective actions observed or recommended. The Environmental Monitor shall be retained and approved by the TDEQ no later than thirty (30) days prior to construction commencement.

**Condition 18: Modification and Amendment**

Any modification to the Project design, layout, construction methods, construction schedule, or operational parameters that could materially alter the environmental impacts assessed in the Environmental Impact Statement or affect Clearwater\'s ability to comply with the conditions of this Order shall require prior written approval of the TDEQ. Requests for modification shall be submitted to the TDEQ in writing and shall include a detailed description of the proposed change, an assessment of the potential environmental impacts of the proposed change, a comparison to the impacts assessed in the EIS, and proposed mitigation measures, if applicable. The TDEQ shall review each modification request and respond in writing within thirty (30) business days of receipt of a complete submission. Clearwater shall not implement any modification subject to this Condition until written approval has been received from the TDEQ.

**Condition 19: Enforcement**

Violation of any condition of this Order may result in enforcement action by the TDEQ, including but not limited to the issuance of a stop-work order requiring the immediate cessation of all or specified construction or operational activities; assessment of civil penalties up to Ten Thousand Dollars (\$10,000.00) per day per violation pursuant to T.S.A. § 27A-1-401; the requirement for implementation of additional or enhanced mitigation measures at Clearwater\'s expense; or revocation of this environmental compliance approval. Clearwater shall be afforded written notice specifying the nature of the alleged violation and an opportunity to cure any non-willful violation within thirty (30) days of receipt of such notice before the imposition of civil penalties, except in cases involving an imminent threat to public health, safety, or the environment, in which case the TDEQ may take immediate enforcement action without prior notice and opportunity to cure.

**Condition 20: Transferability**

This Order, and all obligations and conditions set forth herein, are not transferable to any successor, assignee, purchaser, or other transferee of the Project or any portion thereof without the prior written consent of the TDEQ. Any request for transfer shall be submitted to the TDEQ in writing and shall include evidence satisfactory to the TDEQ that the proposed transferee has the technical expertise and financial capability to comply with all conditions of this Order for the remaining duration of its effectiveness.

**Condition 21: Term and Expiration**

This Order shall remain in effect for the duration of the construction period and for a period of five (5) years following the Commercial Operation Date, except for individual conditions that specify a different duration. By way of example and not limitation, the avian mortality monitoring program under Condition 12 shall be conducted for a period of three (3) years following the Commercial Operation Date. Following the expiration of this Order, Clearwater shall remain subject to all generally applicable TDEQ regulations, environmental standards, and any separate operating permits, discharge permits, or other authorizations that may be required for the ongoing operation of the Facility.

**Condition 22: Severability**

If any provision or condition of this Order is found by a court of competent jurisdiction or other duly authorized body to be invalid, unlawful, or unenforceable, such finding shall not affect the validity or enforceability of the remaining provisions and conditions of this Order, which shall remain in full force and effect.

**Condition 23: Notices**

All notices, reports, submissions, and communications required or permitted under this Order shall be in writing and shall be submitted to the following:

**To the TDEQ:**

> Rebecca Tannenbaum, Environmental Review Specialist Talmadge Department of Environmental Quality 2100 Environmental Way Ashford, Talmadge 73403

**To Clearwater:**

> Priya Venkataraman, General Counsel Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC 900 Commerce Tower, Suite 2200 Ashford, Talmadge 73401

Either party may change its designated notice recipient or address by providing written notice to the other party in accordance with this Condition. Notices shall be deemed effective upon receipt by certified mail, hand delivery, or electronic mail transmission with confirmed receipt.

**UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION** **FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION**

Southwest Regional Office Obstruction Evaluation Group 3100 Aerospace Boulevard Fort Worth, TX 76137

**DETERMINATION OF NO HAZARD TO AIR NAVIGATION**

Aeronautical Study No.: **2024-ASW-8851-OE**

Date of Issuance: **September 27, 2024**

Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC

Attn: Marcus Reyes, Chief Executive Officer

900 Commerce Tower, Suite 2200 Ashford, Talmadge 73401

**Re:** Aeronautical Study No. 2024-ASW-8851-OE --- Ridgeline Solar & Storage Facility, Harmon County, Talmadge

**[Section 1: Introduction and Study Summary]{.underline}**

The Federal Aviation Administration (\"FAA\") conducted an aeronautical study pursuant to the provisions of 49 U.S.C. § 44718 and Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (\"CFR\"), Part 77, Subpart C, concerning proposed structures associated with the Ridgeline Solar & Storage Facility (the \"Project\") in Harmon County, Talmadge. This study was initiated on April 10, 2024, based upon FAA Form 7460-1, Notice of Proposed Construction or Alteration, filed by Clearwater Energy Holdings LLC (\"Clearwater\" or the \"Proponent\"), a Delaware limited liability company registered to do business in the State of Talmadge.

The Project consists of the construction and operation of a 250-megawatt alternating current (250 MW AC) solar photovoltaic generating facility with an associated 100 MW / 400 MWh battery energy storage system (\"BESS\"), together with a project substation and a 345 kilovolt (\"kV\") gen-tie transmission line of approximately 4.7 miles connecting the project substation to the Harmon County Substation operated by Midplains Transmission Co. (the \"Gen-Tie Line\"). The Project is located on approximately 1,850 acres situated in Sections 14, 15, 22, and 23, Township 3 North, Range 24 West, Indian Meridian, Harmon County, Talmadge.

As described in the Form 7460-1 filing and supplemental materials provided by the Proponent, the Gen-Tie Line route crosses two county roads --- County Road 118 (\"CR-118\") and County Road 204 (\"CR-204\") --- and one perennial stream, Willow Creek, a tributary of the Red Fork River. The Gen-Tie Line route was selected by the Proponent to minimize overall length and avoid residential structures while maintaining adequate clearance from existing electrical infrastructure in the area.

The FAA notes that the Proponent has also filed for, or obtained, a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (\"CPCN\") from the Talmadge Public Utilities Commission (Docket No. PUC-2024-0347) and environmental approvals from the Talmadge Department of Environmental Quality (Environmental Compliance Order No. ENV-2024-1192). This aeronautical study is independent of those proceedings and addresses only the effect of the proposed structures on the safe and efficient use of navigable airspace.

The FAA received and considered comments from interested parties during the public comment period, which closed on June 24, 2024. No substantive objections were received. The study was completed on September 20, 2024, and this Determination is issued on September 27, 2024.

**[Section 2: Proposed Structure Heights and Descriptions]{.underline}**

The aeronautical study evaluated the following proposed structures associated with the Project:

**Solar Arrays.** The Project includes single-axis tracker systems with bifacial photovoltaic modules to be installed across approximately 1,450 acres within the Project boundary. The maximum structure height of the solar arrays, at full tilt, is **15 feet above ground level (\"AGL\")**. The solar arrays are distributed across a broad area within Sections 14, 15, 22, and 23 at site elevations ranging from approximately 1,540 to 1,610 feet above mean sea level (\"AMSL\").

**Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Enclosures.** The BESS component consists of 50 containerized battery enclosures to be sited on approximately 12 acres adjacent to the project substation. The maximum height of the BESS enclosures is approximately **12 feet AGL**, which is well below the 14 CFR Part 77 notification threshold for structures under 200 feet AGL located outside the immediate vicinity of an airport.

**Project Substation.** The project substation will include bus structures, step-up power transformers, switchgear, control buildings, and lightning masts. The maximum structure height within the substation footprint is **up to 80 feet AGL**, attributable to the lightning masts and dead-end bus structures. The substation is located at approximately 34°51\'18\"N latitude, 99°48\'42\"W longitude, at a site elevation of approximately 1,580 feet AMSL.

**Gen-Tie Transmission Line Structures.** The Gen-Tie Line consists of steel monopole and lattice structures supporting a 345 kV single-circuit transmission line extending approximately 4.7 miles from the project substation to the existing Harmon County Substation operated by Midplains Transmission Co. The maximum height of the Gen-Tie Line structures is **180 feet AGL**. The tallest proposed monopole structures are located at approximately 34°52\'05\"N latitude, 99°47\'28\"W longitude, at site elevations of approximately 1,575 to 1,590 feet AMSL, resulting in maximum tip elevations of up to approximately 1,770 feet AMSL. The Gen-Tie Line route crosses two county roads (CR-118 and CR-204) and one perennial stream (Willow Creek), with the Willow Creek crossing requiring monopole structures on either bank with a spanning conductor.

**Temporary Construction Cranes.** The Proponent indicated in its filing that construction cranes with boom heights potentially exceeding **200 feet AGL** may be used during the erection of Gen-Tie Line structures and the installation of heavy substation equipment. Such cranes are anticipated to be temporary in nature and would be present on-site during discrete construction phases.

The coordinates provided for the tallest proposed permanent structures --- the Gen-Tie Line monopoles --- are referenced above. The site elevation across the Project area averages approximately 1,580 feet AMSL.

**[Section 3: Aeronautical Study Findings]{.underline}**

The FAA evaluated the proposed structures described in Section 2 for potential hazard to air navigation under the obstruction standards codified at 14 CFR Part 77, Subpart C. The analysis considered the following factors:

**Proximity to Public-Use Airports and Heliports.** The FAA determined that no public-use airport or heliport is located within the relevant notification distances prescribed by 14 CFR § 77.9 for the proposed structure heights. The nearest public-use airport is Hollis Municipal Airport (airport identifier: 85F), a general aviation facility located approximately 18 nautical miles to the northeast of the Project site. At this distance, the proposed structures --- including the Gen-Tie Line structures at up to 180 feet AGL --- do not penetrate any airport imaginary surfaces as defined in 14 CFR § 77.19. No public-use heliport is located within 10 nautical miles of the Project site.

**Military Operations Areas and Training Routes.** The Project site is not located within a designated military operations area (\"MOA\"), restricted area, or military training route. The FAA coordinated with the Department of Defense, as required by 14 CFR Part 77, and received no objection to the proposed structures. The Department of Defense Siting Clearinghouse confirmed that the proposed structures would not adversely affect military operations or readiness.

**Instrument Approach and Departure Procedures.** The FAA reviewed all published instrument approach procedures and departure procedures for airports in the vicinity of the Project site. No conflicts were identified. The proposed structures would not affect any existing or planned instrument flight procedures.

**Visual Flight Rules (VFR) Traffic Patterns.** The FAA evaluated VFR traffic patterns and sectional aeronautical chart depictions in the vicinity of the Project site. No conflicts were identified. The Project site is located in Class G (uncontrolled) airspace, and the proposed structures would not adversely affect VFR operations in the area.

Based on this analysis, the FAA determined that the proposed structures at their stated locations and heights would not exceed obstruction standards under 14 CFR § 77.17 and would not constitute a hazard to air navigation, provided the conditions set forth in Section 5 of this Determination are met.

The FAA notes that the solar arrays at 15 feet AGL are well below the 200-foot AGL notification threshold applicable in most areas and were studied as part of the comprehensive Project filing. The Gen-Tie Line structures at up to 180 feet AGL exceed the 150-foot AGL threshold established by FAA Advisory Circular 70/7460-1M for purposes of obstruction marking and lighting, and specific marking and lighting requirements are set forth in Condition 2 below.

**Solar Glare Analysis.** The FAA also considered the potential for solar glare from the photovoltaic panels to affect aviation safety. Based on the Proponent\'s preliminary glare analysis submitted with the Form 7460-1, and considering the significant distance of the Project site from the nearest air traffic control tower and public-use airport (approximately 18 nautical miles), the FAA concluded that glare from the Project would not constitute a hazard to air navigation. This glare assessment is separate from and does not address any glare study that may be required by the Talmadge Public Utilities Commission or any other regulatory authority as part of the CPCN or other permitting proceedings.

**[Section 4: Determination]{.underline}**

**DETERMINATION:** Based upon the aeronautical study conducted pursuant to Aeronautical Study No. 2024-ASW-8851-OE, the FAA hereby determines that the proposed structures described in Section 2 of this Determination, as part of the Ridgeline Solar & Storage Facility in Harmon County, Talmadge, would **not be a hazard to air navigation**, provided the conditions and limitations set forth in Section 5 of this Determination are satisfied in full.

This Determination is issued pursuant to 49 U.S.C. § 44718 and 14 CFR Part 77. It does not constitute FAA approval or disapproval of the proposed construction. Rather, it is a determination concerning the effect of the proposed structures on the safe and efficient use of navigable airspace by aircraft and on the operation of air navigation facilities.

This Determination does not relieve the Proponent from complying with any requirement imposed by any other federal, state, or local governmental entity with jurisdiction over the Project, including but not limited to the Talmadge Public Utilities Commission, the Talmadge Department of Environmental Quality, the Harmon County Board of Commissioners, or any other agency or authority. This Determination is limited in scope to the aeronautical considerations described herein.

**[Section 5: Conditions and Limitations]{.underline}**

The Determination set forth in Section 4 is subject to the following conditions and limitations:

**Condition 1 --- Maximum Structure Heights.**

The maximum heights of the proposed structures shall not exceed the following limits:

> \(a\) **Solar arrays:** Maximum height of **15 feet AGL**.
>
> \(b\) **Project substation:** Maximum height of **80 feet AGL**, including all bus structures, transformers, lightning masts, and associated equipment.
>
> \(c\) **Gen-Tie transmission line structures:** Maximum height of **180 feet AGL**.
>
> \(d\) **BESS enclosures:** Maximum height of **15 feet AGL**.

Any increase in the maximum heights stated herein, or any material change in the location or configuration of the proposed structures, will require the filing of a new FAA Form 7460-1 and the completion of a new aeronautical study. This Determination applies only to structures at or below the heights specified above.

**Condition 2 --- Obstruction Marking and Lighting.**

All structures exceeding **150 feet AGL** must be equipped with FAA-compliant obstruction lighting in accordance with **FAA Advisory Circular 70/7460-1M**, \"Obstruction Marking and Lighting,\" as in effect at the time of construction. This requirement applies to the Gen-Tie transmission line structures at up to 180 feet AGL. Obstruction lighting must be operational prior to any such structure reaching its maximum height, or as soon as practicable thereafter if temporary marking measures are employed during the construction period. The recommended lighting type is medium-intensity dual obstruction lights (red/white), as specified in the current edition of AC 70/7460-1M, unless an alternative marking or lighting scheme is approved in writing by the FAA.

**Condition 3 --- FAA Form 7460-2 Filing (Notice of Actual Construction).**

The Proponent shall file **FAA Form 7460-2**, Notice of Actual Construction or Alteration, **within five (5) days** after each structure exceeding **150 feet AGL** reaches its greatest height. This filing must be submitted electronically through the FAA\'s Obstruction Evaluation / Airport Airspace Analysis (OE/AAA) system at https://oeaaa.faa.gov. This post-construction notification is required for each Gen-Tie Line structure that reaches or exceeds 150 feet AGL and must include the as-built height and geographic coordinates of the structure.

**Condition 4 --- Construction Cranes --- Separate Aeronautical Study.**

Any construction cranes or other temporary structures exceeding **200 feet AGL** require a **separate** FAA Form 7460-1 filing and a separate aeronautical study prior to use. Such filing must be made at least **forty-five (45) days in advance** of the planned deployment of such crane or temporary structure to allow adequate time for the FAA to complete its review. The Proponent should coordinate with the FAA Southwest Regional Office, Obstruction Evaluation Group, at 3100 Aerospace Boulevard, Fort Worth, TX 76137, regarding the scheduling and sequencing of crane operations, particularly during the erection of Gen-Tie Line structures.

**Condition 5 --- Construction Commencement Deadline.**

**This Determination expires and is no longer valid if construction of the proposed structures that are the subject of this study is not started on or before March 27, 2026** (eighteen (18) months from the date of this Determination, September 27, 2024). For purposes of this condition, \"construction \... is not started\" means that physical construction work on the structure itself --- such as foundation excavation, tower erection, or comparable physical activity directly related to the construction of the structure --- has not begun. This condition applies to the proposed structures that are the subject of this study, which include but are not limited to the Gen-Tie transmission line structures (the tallest permanent structures at up to 180 feet AGL). If the Determination expires under this condition, the Proponent may request a new aeronautical study by filing a new FAA Form 7460-1.

**Condition 6 --- Construction Completion Deadline.**

**This Determination also expires if the construction of the tallest structures is not completed on or before March 27, 2027** (thirty (30) months from the date of this Determination, September 27, 2024). For purposes of this condition, \"completed\" means that the structures have reached their final, as-built height and are no longer under active vertical construction. If construction is not completed by this date, a new aeronautical study may be required, and the Proponent should contact the FAA to determine whether a new filing is necessary.

**Condition 7 --- Notification of Changes.**

If there are any changes to the proposed structures, including but not limited to changes in location, height, number, or configuration, the Proponent must notify the FAA by filing a new or revised FAA Form 7460-1 for a new aeronautical study. Changes to the Gen-Tie Line route, the addition of structures not previously evaluated, or the relocation of the project substation would each require separate notification and study. The Proponent bears the responsibility to ensure that the structures as built are consistent with the structures as described in the original Form 7460-1 filing.

**Condition 8 --- Coordination with Local Authorities.**

This Determination is issued on the basis that the proposed structures will be constructed and operated in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements. The Proponent is advised to coordinate with the Harmon County Board of Commissioners and any other local governmental entity with jurisdiction over the Project site regarding local building codes, road crossing permits, and other land use approvals. The Proponent is also advised that separate approvals may be required from the Talmadge Public Utilities Commission (CPCN proceedings) and the Talmadge Department of Environmental Quality (environmental compliance), and that this FAA Determination does not satisfy or substitute for any such requirements.

**[Section 6: Expiration and Renewal]{.underline}**

This Determination expires under either of the following circumstances:

> \(a\) Construction of the proposed structures that are the subject of this study is not started on or before **March 27, 2026** (eighteen (18) months from the date of issuance); or
>
> \(b\) Construction of the tallest proposed structures is not completed on or before **March 27, 2027** (thirty (30) months from the date of issuance).

If this Determination expires under either scenario, the Proponent may request a new aeronautical study by filing a new FAA Form 7460-1 through the OE/AAA system. Any new study will be conducted based on conditions existing at the time of the new filing, including any changes to airport facilities, airspace designations, instrument procedures, or obstruction standards that may have occurred in the interim.

This Determination is not subject to extension. The deadlines set forth in Conditions 5 and 6 are firm and may not be waived or modified except through the issuance of a new determination based on a new aeronautical study. However, if construction has commenced but circumstances have changed materially --- such as a significant design modification or an unforeseen construction delay --- the Proponent should contact the FAA Southwest Regional Office to discuss whether a revised study or supplemental filing is warranted.

**[Section 7: Additional Advisory Information]{.underline}**

The FAA notes that this Determination addresses only the effect of the proposed structures on air navigation and the safe and efficient use of navigable airspace. It does not address electromagnetic interference, environmental impacts, wildlife considerations, noise, visual aesthetics, or any other non-aeronautical considerations that may be relevant to the permitting or construction of the Project.

The Proponent should be aware that solar photovoltaic installations may produce glare that could affect pilots operating aircraft in the vicinity. While the FAA\'s aeronautical study determined that glare from the proposed Project would not constitute a hazard to air navigation based on the Project\'s significant distance from airports and established flight paths, the Proponent may wish to consider the use of anti-reflective coatings or panel surface treatments to minimize potential glare effects on low-altitude aviation operations, particularly agricultural aviation. This recommendation is advisory only and is not a condition of this Determination.

The Proponent should also be aware that this Determination is based entirely on the information provided in the Form 7460-1 filing dated April 10, 2024, and supplemental materials submitted thereafter. Any material changes to the Project that were not reflected in the original filing must be reported to the FAA as described in Condition 7 above.

Questions regarding this Determination, requests for clarification, or inquiries concerning future filings should be directed to the FAA Southwest Regional Office, Obstruction Evaluation Group, at the following address:

> Federal Aviation Administration Southwest Regional Office Obstruction Evaluation Group 3100 Aerospace Boulevard Fort Worth, TX 76137 Telephone: (817) 555-4200
>
> Email: OEGroup-ASW@faa.gov

**[Section 8: Signature]{.underline}**

This Determination is issued by the undersigned on behalf of the Federal Aviation Administration, Southwest Regional Office.

"Do not file a notice that lacks the IA. ("2","IA execution deadline of January 16, 2025 versus memo target of \"early Q1 2025\": CPCN revocation risk; financial close and gen-tie gated",

The Order itself warns (§V.F) that its definition may differ from commercial definitions.",
"Run two COD tracks in the compliance calendar. Set a \"CPCN COD\" milestone at first grid delivery, including test energy, and a \"TDEQ COD\" milestone at full commissioning. Prepare the 10-business-day COD notice, the bond, the community benefit fund payment and the avian program on the CPCN track. Revise the memo's post-COD milestones before the schedule goes to Stonebridge."),
("4","BESS commissioning sequence conflicts with the fire-suppression certification and ERP deadlines",
"TDEQ Condition 15 requires independent certification by a Talmadge-licensed fire protection engineer \"prior to the energization of any BESS component.\" A copy must be filed with TDEQ at least 15 days before BESS energization. The memo schedules electrical integration with the substation, PCS testing and HVAC commissioning for January to March 2026, and charge/discharge cycling for April to June 2026. "Move the third-party certification before the first energization of any BESS component (target November to December 2025). File the certification with TDEQ at least 15 days before that energization, and file the ERP at least 60 days before it (about early November 2025 for a January 2026 energization). Alternatively, defer all BESS energization until after a May 2026 certification and re-sequence commissioning. Confirm that the 50,000-gallon fire water supply and hydrants are installed before energization."),
("5","Decommissioning bond: the amount in Condition 14 is inconsistent with the Order's findings",
"Finding 24 and §V.E require the bond to be \"not less than the estimated decommissioning cost\" of $19,200,000. Condition 14, however, sets the bond at $18,500,000, which is $700,000 short. The memo does not state an amount. The rehearing or reconsideration window (30 days from October 18, 2024) ends on November 17, 2024, a Sunday. The timing issue in Issue 3 also applies: the bond is due 12 months after CPCN COD, not 12 months after the commercial COD.",
"Before November 17, 2024 (next business day, November 18), decide whether to file a motion for clarification or seek an errata from TPUC. Absent clarification, plan to post at least $19.2 million so that both the Condition 14 amount and the findings are satisfied. "Before inverter and BESS HVAC procurement is final, commission updated acoustic modeling at the Pullman property line and at other non-participating boundaries. "Finalize and submit the screening plan (species, sizes, spacing, density, irrigation, maintenance) by December 2, 2024, or move planting later. Seek written clarification from TDEQ and Harmon County on whether the buffer and setback overlap, and design to the more restrictive result (CPCN Condition 22)."),
("8","Pre-construction biological surveys: the memo omits the 30-day submittal rule and the separate surveys required for each area",
"Under TDEQ Condition 2, a survey must be conducted no earlier than 60 days before ground disturbance and submitted to TDEQ (attention R. Tannenbaum) no later than 30 days before ground disturbance. Under CPCN Condition 19, results must be filed with TDEQ and TPUC within 10 business days of completion. "Get TDEQ approval of the biologist now. Schedule each survey within its 60-to-30-day window, keyed to the actual disturbance date. Build a survey matrix by area and phase, with the gen-tie survey in February to March 2025 for an April start. File results with TPUC within 10 business days."),
("9","Several TDEQ deliverables due before construction commencement are missing from the memo; SWPPP approval has no float",
"Before construction commencement, defined in TDEQ Finding 8 as any ground disturbance, the following must be completed: the SWPPP must be submitted at least 30 days before and approved in writing before commencement (TDEQ review takes 15 business days; a December 15, 2024 submission gives an approval date of about January 7, 2025 if there are no revisions); the HMMP must be submitted at least 30 days before (Condition 11); the Unanticipated Discovery Plan must be prepared with SHPO and approved by TDEQ (Condition 14); the Environmental Monitor must be retained and TDEQ-approved at least 30 days before (Condition 17); erosion and sediment controls must be operational (Condition 7); and the wetland delineation must be completed (Condition 8). Only the SWPPP appears in the memo. Also required: TDEQ notice within 5 business days after commencement (Condition 16); CGL insurance of $5M/$10M naming TPUC, the State and the County as additional insureds (CPCN Condition 23); and road-crossing permits filed with TPUC before gen-tie construction (CPCN Condition 16).",
"Add each item to the pre-NTP checklist with an owner. Submit the SWPPP and HMMP by early December 2024 to leave room for one revision cycle. Nominate the Environmental Monitor to TDEQ in November 2024."),
("10","Willow Creek and gen-tie sequencing: the TDEQ restriction covers the whole riparian corridor, not only in-stream work",
"TDEQ Condition 3 limits all activity within 100 feet of the ordinary high water mark (clearing, grading, staging, structure installation) to June 1 through September 30. It also requires continuous upstream and downstream turbidity monitoring with weekly reports to TDEQ, a stop-work and 24-hour notice for any exceedance of +50 NTU, and no permanent structures below the high water mark. CPCN Condition 20 requires disturbed streambanks to be restored within 30 days after the crossing is complete. That restoration is itself corridor work and must also finish by September 30 unless TDEQ authorizes otherwise in writing. The memo describes the window as applying to \"in-stream work\" and starts gen-tie work in April 2025. Any work within 100 feet of Willow Creek before June 1 is prohibited. If the crossing slips past about August 31, restoration may not fit inside the window. If 2025 is missed, the next window is June 2026, which would threaten the FAA and CPCN dates and COD.",
"Exclude the 100-foot corridor from the April to May gen-tie work fronts. Complete the crossing by about August 15 and restoration by September 30, 2025. ("11","Dust monitoring network does not meet the ECO",
"TDEQ Condition 5 requires at least four PM10 stations, one on each cardinal side (north, south, east and west). "Install four or more stations before ground disturbance, get TDEQ approval of the suppressants, and adopt an exceedance response protocol."),
("12","FAA and CPCN structure and airspace discrepancies",

The memo's glare scope refers to Vance Municipal Airport about 6.2 miles southeast. "Confirm the substation design is 80 feet or lower. Verify the Vance Municipal Airport status and location and, if it is public-use, consult the FAA Southwest Regional Office (Condition 7). "Obtain and review the SUP, then add its conditions to this matrix before the construction management plan and the Stonebridge diligence package are finalized."),
]
