Any test energy delivered to the grid would trigger CPCN COD, possibly in Q2 or Q3 2026. Every CPCN COD-linked date then moves earlier: the COD notice (10 business days); the decommissioning bond (12 months, so about July 2027, not Dec. 1, 2027); the first $150,000 community benefit fund payment (about July 2027); the start of the avian monitoring term under CPCN Condition 21; and the obligations tied to start of operations (Condition 7 glare mitigation, Condition 17 screening). The Order itself warns (§V.F) that the regulatory definition may differ from commercial definitions.",
"Run two COD tracks in the compliance calendar: \"CPCN COD\" (first grid delivery, including test energy) and \"TDEQ COD\" (full commissioning). Before energization, confirm with Midplains and TPUC Staff whether test energy counts. Put the 10-business-day COD notice, the bond, the community benefit fund payment and avian monitoring on the CPCN track. Correct the memo's post-COD milestones before the schedule goes to Stonebridge."),
("4","BESS commissioning sequence conflicts with fire-suppression certification and ERP deadlines",
"TDEQ Condition 15 requires certification by an independent, Talmadge-licensed fire protection engineer \"prior to the energization of any BESS component.\" The certification must be filed with TDEQ at least 15 days before BESS energization. The BESS Emergency Response Plan (ERP) must be submitted to TDEQ and the Harmon County Fire Department for approval at least 60 days before energization. The memo schedules electrical integration with the substation, PCS testing and HVAC commissioning for January to March 2026, and charge/discharge cycling for April to June 2026. Both involve energizing BESS components, yet certification is scheduled for May 2026 and the ERP is not mentioned. Energizing 4 or more months before certification would violate the ECO and expose Clearwater to a stop-work order and civil penalties of up to $10,000 per day per violation (TDEQ Condition 19).",
"Move third-party certification ahead of the first energization of any BESS component (target Nov.–Dec. 2025). File the certification with TDEQ at least 15 days before, and the ERP at least 60 days before (about early Nov. 2025 for a January 2026 energization). Alternatively, hold all BESS energization until after a May 2026 certification and re-sequence commissioning. Confirm the 50,000-gallon fire water supply and hydrants are in place before energization."),
("5","Decommissioning bond amount in Condition 14 ($18.5M) is inconsistent with the Order's findings ($19.2M)",
"Finding 24 and §V.E require a bond \"not less than the estimated decommissioning cost\" of $19,200,000. Condition 14 sets the bond at $18,500,000, which is $700,000 short. The memo does not state an amount. The 30-day rehearing/reconsideration window from October 18, 2024 closes November 17, 2024 (a Sunday). The timing point in Issue 3 also applies: the bond is due within 12 months of CPCN COD, not 12 months after the commercial COD.",
"Decide by Nov. 17, 2024 (next business day Nov. 18) whether to file a motion for clarification or request an errata from TPUC. Absent clarification, plan to post at least $19.2M, which satisfies both the condition and the findings. Size the letter-of-credit facility in the financing model: issuer rated A- or better, form approved by TPUC General Counsel, TPUC as trustee. Calendar the 5-year adjustments."),
("6","Operational noise limit applies at the property line; the noise study modeled the residence",
"CPCN Condition 8 sets a 45 dBA (Leq, 1-hour) not-to-exceed limit \"measured at the property line of the nearest non-participating residence.\" The Pullman property adjoins the northern boundary of Sections 14 and 15, so its property line is the Project boundary. The Henley study predicts 42 dBA (typical) and 44 dBA (worst case) at the residence, about 900 feet from the nearest array (Finding 13). Levels at the shared boundary will be higher. The memo assumes compliance at \"property-line measurement points\" without new modeling. On a complaint, Clearwater must take measurements within 30 days, file results within 15 days, and cure within 90 days.",
"Commission updated acoustic modeling at the Pullman property line and other non-participating boundaries before inverter and BESS HVAC procurement is final. Site inverters and BESS HVAC away from the northern boundary as needed. Equipment changes may trigger the ISIS reactive-power test (CPCN Condition 6, more than 5% change) and TDEQ Condition 18."),
("7","Vegetative screening plan is due about Dec. 2, 2024 and is not in the memo",
"TDEQ Condition 6 requires the screening plan to be submitted for TDEQ approval at least 60 days before planting begins. Planting must be completed before solar array installation begins in Sections 14 and 15, must reach 80% opacity within 3 years (certified by a licensed landscape architect), and must be at least 50 feet wide along the entire northern boundary. The memo starts planting in February to March 2025, \"weather permitting,\" so the plan is due by about December 2, 2024 for a February 1 planting start. CPCN Condition 17 separately requires installation before Facility operations. How the 50-foot buffer relates to the SUP's 75-foot setback is unresolved (CPCN §V.C).",
"Finalize and submit the screening plan (species, sizes, spacing, density, irrigation, maintenance) by Dec. 2, 2024, or move planting later. Make completed planting a hard predecessor to tracker and module installation in Sections 14 and 15. Get written clarification from TDEQ and Harmon County on whether the buffer and setback overlap, and design to the more restrictive outcome (CPCN Condition 22)."),
("8","Pre-construction biological surveys: memo omits the 30-day submittal rule and the per-area survey requirement",
"TDEQ Condition 2 requires each survey to be conducted no earlier than 60 days before ground disturbance and submitted to TDEQ (attn. R. Tannenbaum) no later than 30 days before ground disturbance. The biologist must be approved by TDEQ in advance. A separate survey is required for each phase and each discrete area. CPCN Condition 19 requires results to be filed with TDEQ and TPUC within 10 business days of completion. For a February 1, 2025 start, the survey window is December 3, 2024 to about January 2, 2025, with submittal due January 2, 2025. The memo's \"late December\" target leaves almost no margin, and any slip in the start date (Issue 1) makes the survey stale. The memo addresses only Phase 1. The off-site gen-tie corridor, the Willow Creek riparian corridor, the substation/BESS pad and each laydown yard need their own timely surveys.",
"Obtain TDEQ approval of the biologist now. Schedule each survey within its 60-to-30-day window, keyed to the actual disturbance date. Build a survey matrix by area and phase, including a gen-tie survey in Feb.–Mar. 2025 for an April start. File results with TPUC within 10 business days."),
("9","TDEQ pre-commencement deliverables missing from the memo; SWPPP approval has no float",
"Before construction commencement (any ground disturbance, TDEQ Finding 8): the SWPPP must be submitted at least 30 days before and approved in writing before commencement (TDEQ review takes 15 business days, so a Dec. 15, 2024 submission yields approval on about Jan. 7, 2025 if no revisions are requested); the HMMP must be submitted at least 30 days before (Condition 11); the Unanticipated Discovery Plan must be prepared with SHPO and approved by TDEQ (Condition 14); the Environmental Monitor must be retained and approved by TDEQ at least 30 days before (Condition 17); erosion and sediment controls must be operational (Condition 7); and the wetland delineation must be complete (Condition 8). Only the SWPPP appears in the memo. Also required: notice to TDEQ within 5 business days after commencement (Condition 16); CGL insurance of $5M per occurrence / $10M aggregate naming TPUC, the State and the County as additional insureds (CPCN Condition 23); and road-crossing permits filed with TPUC before gen-tie construction (CPCN Condition 16).",
"Add each item to the pre-NTP checklist with an owner. Submit the SWPPP and HMMP by early December 2024 to leave room for one revision cycle. Nominate the Environmental Monitor to TDEQ in November 2024."),
("10","Willow Creek / gen-tie sequencing: TDEQ restriction covers the entire 100-ft riparian corridor, not only in-stream work",
"TDEQ Condition 3 limits all activity within 100 feet of the ordinary high water mark (clearing, grading, staging, structure installation) to June 1 through September 30. It also requires continuous upstream and downstream turbidity monitoring with weekly reports to TDEQ, a stop-work order and 24-hour notice for any exceedance of +50 NTU, and no permanent structures below the high water mark. CPCN Condition 20 requires disturbed streambanks to be restored within 30 days of completing the crossing. That restoration is itself corridor work and must also finish by September 30 unless TDEQ authorizes otherwise in writing. The memo describes the window as applying to \"in-stream work\" and starts gen-tie work in April 2025, but any work within 100 feet of Willow Creek before June 1 is prohibited. If the crossing runs past about August 31, restoration may not fit within the window. If the 2025 window is missed, the next window opens June 2026, which threatens the FAA and CPCN dates and COD.",
"Exclude the 100-ft corridor from the April–May gen-tie work fronts. Target completion of the crossing by about Aug. 15, 2025 and restoration by Sept. 30, 2025. Mobilize turbidity monitoring and the weekly reporting protocol before June 1. Maintain the 50-ft setback from delineated wetlands along the gen-tie alignment."),
("11","Dust monitoring network does not meet the ECO",
"TDEQ Condition 5 requires at least four PM10 stations, one on each cardinal side (north, south, east and west). It also requires TDEQ approval of chemical suppressants, a halt of dust-generating work within 500 feet of any reading above 150 µg/m³, and notice to TDEQ within 24 hours. The memo proposes stations only on the northern and eastern boundaries and proposes magnesium chloride \"or equivalent\" without TDEQ approval.",
"Install at least four stations before ground disturbance, obtain TDEQ approval of the suppressants, and adopt an exceedance-response protocol."),
("12","FAA / CPCN structure and airspace discrepancies",
"(a) FAA Condition 1(b) caps the project substation at 80 ft AGL; CPCN Condition 13(b) allows 180 ft. The FAA limit governs, and the memo does not mention it. (b) FAA Condition 1(d) caps BESS enclosures at 15 ft. (c) The FAA states the nearest public-use airport is Hollis Municipal (85F), about 18 nm northeast, and that no public-use airport is within notification distances. The memo's glare scope refers to Vance Municipal Airport about 6.2 miles southeast. Because the FAA determination rests \"entirely\" on the Form 7460-1 information (Section 7), an omitted nearby airport is a validity risk. (d) The CPCN describes the gen-tie as steel monopoles; the memo and the FAA describe monopole and lattice structures. (e) Cranes above 200 ft AGL are also expected for heavy substation equipment, not only gen-tie erection. Each needs a separate Form 7460-1 at least 45 days in advance, may not be deployed until the FAA issues a determination (CPCN Condition 15), and requires concurrent notice to TPUC. (f) Obstruction lighting must be operational before each structure over 150 ft reaches full height, and Form 7460-2 must be filed within 5 days.",
"Confirm the substation design is 80 ft or lower. Verify Vance Municipal Airport's status and location and, if it is public-use, consult the FAA Southwest Regional Office (Condition 7). Confirm the CPCN record covers lattice structures or notify TPUC (Conditions 1 and 24). Add substation cranes to the FAA filing schedule."),
("13","Harmon County SUP not provided, although its conditions are incorporated into the CPCN",
"CPCN Condition 22 incorporates SUP No. HC-2024-0038 by reference, makes any SUP violation a CPCN violation, and applies the more restrictive requirement in any conflict. The CPCN describes the 75-ft setback only as \"reported\" and \"as represented by the Applicant.\" The SUP's road-improvement, dust and screening conditions could not be extracted for this matrix.",
"Obtain and review the SUP, and add its conditions to this matrix before the construction management plan and the Stonebridge diligence package are finalized."),
]
PYEOF
); $S $R "echo $B | base64 -d > /workspace/build/crit.py && python3 -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0,\"/workspace/build\"); import crit; print(len(crit.CRIT))'"

def table(headers, rows, widths, status_col=None, fs=8):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers)); t.style = "Table Grid"; t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    t.autofit = False
    hdr = t.rows[0]; rep_header(hdr)
    for i,h in enumerate(headers):

        shade(c, "1F3A5F")
    for row in rows:
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        for i,v in enumerate(row):
            c = cells[i]; c.text = ""; r = c.paragraphs[0].add_run(str(v)); r.font.size = Pt(fs)
            if i == 0: r.bold = True
            if status_col is not None and i == status_col:

                if v in ("CRITICAL","AT RISK","ONGOING","ALIGNED"): r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xFF,0xFF,0xFF)
    for row in t.rows:
        for i,w in enumerate(widths): row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    # tblGrid widths
    grid = t._tbl.tblGrid
    for i,gc in enumerate(grid.findall(qn("w:gridCol"))): gc.set(qn("w:w"), str(int(widths[i]*1440)))
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return t

The compliance tracking matrix is written to `compliance-tracking-matrix.docx`. It covers 56 conditions from the TPUC CPCN, TDEQ ECO and FAA Determination, checked against the Nov. 12, 2024 project timeline memo, and flags 13 critical issues; the memo's schedule is not compliant as drafted. The file passed the docx validation script and parses back cleanly.

The most urgent findings:
- **TPUC notice and Interconnection Agreement (IA):** the 60-day notice planned for Nov. 15, 2024 must include the signed Midplains IA, which isn't signed yet. The IA itself is due Jan. 16, 2025, after the memo's Jan. 10 financial close. To start on Feb. 1, 2025, the IA must be signed and the notice filed by Dec. 3, 2024. If the IA is signed only on Jan. 16, the earliest compliant start is Mar. 17, 2025.
- **Two meanings of commercial operation date (COD):** the CPCN uses first delivery to the grid, which on the memo's schedule is about July 2026. The bond and first community fund payment then fall due about July 2027, not Dec. 1, 2027. The ECO's full-commissioning date of Dec. 1, 2026 still governs the laydown-yard and avian deadlines.
- **Battery energization:** battery components are energized from January 2026, but the required fire-suppression certification is scheduled for May 2026. The emergency response plan, due 60 days before energization, is missing from the memo.
- **Decommissioning bond:** Condition 14 says $18.5M, but the order's findings require at least the $19.2M estimate. The rehearing window closes Nov. 17/18, 2024.
- **Missing from the memo:**
  - vegetative screening plan, due about Dec. 2, 2024
  - biological surveys for each area, submitted 30 days before ground disturbance
  - hazardous materials plan, discovery plan and environmental monitor
  - four dust monitors instead of two
  - Willow Creek limits covering all work within 100 ft of the creek
  - construction-noise notices
  - road-crossing permits
  - insurance
  - annual mitigation fee
- **Other discrepancies:**
  - the FAA caps the substation at 80 ft, while the CPCN allows 180 ft
  - the memo and FAA disagree on the nearest airport
  - the noise study modeled the residence, but the limit applies at the property line

The Harmon County Special Use Permit wasn't among the documents, so its conditions are not in the matrix even though the CPCN incorporates them. "Start of construction" in the CPCN is treated as first ground disturbance, which TPUC Staff should confirm.
